AppShell.name: AppShell
AppShell.import: import { AppShell, AppShellHeader, AppShellPane, AppShellAction, AppShellAccount } from "@zen-ds/react";
AppShell.purpose: The frame of an app, built on Figma's AppShell patterns. From 1024px (desktops, iPad landscape) a desktop pattern: Sidebar · List-Detail · Top-Bar · Workspace · Docs · Focus · Grid, with Header/AppShell, panes, progress, a docked side panel and floating actions. Narrower, with mobile parts (phones, iPad portrait), a mobile pattern: the TopNavigation as a Bar, a Band with a hero, a Band-Sheet or over Media, then the Tab-Bar, a floating glass bar or an Action bar. Without mobile parts a narrow shell keeps its header and opens the Sidebar as a modal drawer. The Body pads Margin-Comfortable, so the page needs no Container for the margins.
use: Every app screen: one AppShell at the root, inside ZenProvider.

Navigation between a few roots → pattern="sidebar" (the default); a list beside its detail (inbox, requests) → "list-detail"; one company or product without navigation → "top-bar"; tools around a canvas → "workspace"; reading → "docs"; one task with steps → "focus"; the Sidebar workspace drawn in lines (dense dashboards, analytics, admin) → "grid".

A phone or an upright iPad → topNavigation with bottomNavigation (roots) or actionBar (a task's actions); a brand band → mobileTop="band" with hero; a profile or a summary rising over colour → "band-sheet"; a photo, video or map → "media" with backdrop.
Header icon actions with an unread dot or count → AppShellAction; the account menu → Menu with an AppShellAccount trigger.
avoid: Marketing pages → Container + your own header.
A modal flow → Dialog or SidePanel type="modal".
Page actions (Submit, Export, New) → the PageHeader actions in the header's main, not its top row.
A second shell inside a pane or a card → one AppShell per screen.

AreaChart.name: AreaChart
AreaChart.import: import { LineChart, BarChart, StackBarChart, DonutChart, RadialChart, HeatmapChart, BarList, BulletChart, GaugeChart, FunnelChart, AreaChart, GroupedBarChart, ComboChart, ChartCard } from "@zen-ds/react";
AreaChart.purpose: One chart family in one style: how a value changes over time (Line, Area), compares across periods or categories (Bar; 2–3 series side by side: Grouped bar), splits a total (Stack bar, Stacked area, Donut), reads two measures in different units over the same periods (Combo), measures against a maximum (Radial), ranks items (Bar list), tracks goals against their targets (Bullet), reads one measure against its maximum and target (Gauge), follows the drop-off between stages (Funnel) or spreads over two dimensions (Heatmap), framed by a Chart Card with a title, a figure and a range switch. Every chart draws itself in when it mounts and when its data changes.
use: A trend over 4–12 periods → LineChart.
Against last year, the plan or a second measure over the same periods → LineChart compare (one dashed comparison line, with a legend).
Compare periods or categories → BarChart (vertical).
Long category names or a goal per bar → BarChart orientation="horizontal" with target.
A forecast → projected bars.
Part-to-whole across periods → StackBarChart with a legend.
One measure over time where its volume matters as much as its trend (hours, sessions) → AreaChart.
2–4 parts of a total over time → AreaChart type="stacked" (the top line is the total, the legend names the bands).
2–3 measures side by side per period or category (invoiced vs. collected, this year vs. last) → GroupedBarChart with its legend.
Parts of one total → StackBarChart.
Two measures in different units over the same periods (revenue and margin %, hours and utilisation) → ComboChart: bars on the start axis, a line on the end axis.
A share on a fixed 0 – 100% axis → lineMax={100}.
Shares of one total (2–7) → DonutChart.
1–4 measures against the same maximum (budget used, goals) → RadialChart.
A value per day × hour, or any row × column grid → HeatmapChart.
A ranking of 3–8 items with their values (top clients, pages, products) → BarList, ranked largest first: the names sit in the bars, the values line up at the end.
Many rows to sort, filter or export → Table.
1–4 goals against their targets, each in its own unit (revenue, new clients, utilisation) → BulletChart.
Shares of the same maximum as rings → RadialChart.
One progress value → ProgressBar.
One measure against its maximum, with or without a target (utilisation, hours this week) → GaugeChart (several measures on one maximum: RadialChart; a plain progress value: ProgressBar).
3–6 steps where each keeps part of the one before (leads to signed, applications to hires) → FunnelChart, first stage first (categories that aren't steps: BarList or BarChart).
Dashboard tiles → ChartCard (icon, description, value) next to Metric Cards.
A phone screen whose one main chart is the point → the chart straight on the screen, without a Chart Card (its padding costs the plot its width): a heading, a full-width Segmented, the chart.
avoid: One number → Metric / MetricCard.
Exact values to compare or export → Table.
More than ~7 series or slices → split the chart or use a Table.
A donut for values over time → LineChart or BarChart.
One progress value with a label → ProgressBar / ProgressCircle, not a RadialChart.
Values over time, or more than 8 items, in a BarList → BarChart or a Table.
Values without a target in a BulletChart → BarList or BarChart.
A gauge for values over time or for several measures → LineChart, RadialChart or BulletChart.
A funnel for categories, or for stages that grow → BarList or BarChart.
More than 3 series in a GroupedBarChart, or stacked areas whose series aren't parts of one total → StackBarChart, LineChart or a Table.
A ComboChart for two measures in the same unit → GroupedBarChart or LineChart compare.

BarChart.name: BarChart
BarChart.import: import { LineChart, BarChart, StackBarChart, DonutChart, RadialChart, HeatmapChart, BarList, BulletChart, GaugeChart, FunnelChart, AreaChart, GroupedBarChart, ComboChart, ChartCard } from "@zen-ds/react";
BarChart.purpose: One chart family in one style: how a value changes over time (Line, Area), compares across periods or categories (Bar; 2–3 series side by side: Grouped bar), splits a total (Stack bar, Stacked area, Donut), reads two measures in different units over the same periods (Combo), measures against a maximum (Radial), ranks items (Bar list), tracks goals against their targets (Bullet), reads one measure against its maximum and target (Gauge), follows the drop-off between stages (Funnel) or spreads over two dimensions (Heatmap), framed by a Chart Card with a title, a figure and a range switch. Every chart draws itself in when it mounts and when its data changes.
use: A trend over 4–12 periods → LineChart.
Against last year, the plan or a second measure over the same periods → LineChart compare (one dashed comparison line, with a legend).
Compare periods or categories → BarChart (vertical).
Long category names or a goal per bar → BarChart orientation="horizontal" with target.
A forecast → projected bars.
Part-to-whole across periods → StackBarChart with a legend.
One measure over time where its volume matters as much as its trend (hours, sessions) → AreaChart.
2–4 parts of a total over time → AreaChart type="stacked" (the top line is the total, the legend names the bands).
2–3 measures side by side per period or category (invoiced vs. collected, this year vs. last) → GroupedBarChart with its legend.
Parts of one total → StackBarChart.
Two measures in different units over the same periods (revenue and margin %, hours and utilisation) → ComboChart: bars on the start axis, a line on the end axis.
A share on a fixed 0 – 100% axis → lineMax={100}.
Shares of one total (2–7) → DonutChart.
1–4 measures against the same maximum (budget used, goals) → RadialChart.
A value per day × hour, or any row × column grid → HeatmapChart.
A ranking of 3–8 items with their values (top clients, pages, products) → BarList, ranked largest first: the names sit in the bars, the values line up at the end.
Many rows to sort, filter or export → Table.
1–4 goals against their targets, each in its own unit (revenue, new clients, utilisation) → BulletChart.
Shares of the same maximum as rings → RadialChart.
One progress value → ProgressBar.
One measure against its maximum, with or without a target (utilisation, hours this week) → GaugeChart (several measures on one maximum: RadialChart; a plain progress value: ProgressBar).
3–6 steps where each keeps part of the one before (leads to signed, applications to hires) → FunnelChart, first stage first (categories that aren't steps: BarList or BarChart).
Dashboard tiles → ChartCard (icon, description, value) next to Metric Cards.
A phone screen whose one main chart is the point → the chart straight on the screen, without a Chart Card (its padding costs the plot its width): a heading, a full-width Segmented, the chart.
avoid: One number → Metric / MetricCard.
Exact values to compare or export → Table.
More than ~7 series or slices → split the chart or use a Table.
A donut for values over time → LineChart or BarChart.
One progress value with a label → ProgressBar / ProgressCircle, not a RadialChart.
Values over time, or more than 8 items, in a BarList → BarChart or a Table.
Values without a target in a BulletChart → BarList or BarChart.
A gauge for values over time or for several measures → LineChart, RadialChart or BulletChart.
A funnel for categories, or for stages that grow → BarList or BarChart.
More than 3 series in a GroupedBarChart, or stacked areas whose series aren't parts of one total → StackBarChart, LineChart or a Table.
A ComboChart for two measures in the same unit → GroupedBarChart or LineChart compare.

data.description: One bar per category or period (`{ label, value }`); mark a forecast `projected` (hatched) and give a bar a `target` to draw its goal as a hatched track behind it.

orientation.description: `vertical` columns over periods (default) or `horizontal` bars for categories with longer names (Q1–Q4, teams).

height.description: Height of a vertical plot in px, lanes included.

aria-label.description: What the chart shows and over which range ("Revenue per month, Jan – Dec 2026").

initialIndex.description: The bar active at first (painted Chart/Sector/Secondary, its Tooltip shown).

animate.description: Grow the bars from the baseline on mount and when the data changes (default true; reduced motion fades).

A short form or filters (Modal).

Box.name: Box
Box.import: import { Stack, Grid, Box, Container } from "@zen-ds/react";
Box.purpose: Token-based layout primitives: Stack (one direction), Grid (columns), Box (a frame without auto layout) and Container (page width and margin). Stack, Grid and Box are Figma's frames: each takes the fill (background layer), stroke, corner radius, effect style, opacity, rotation and flip, so an auto layout frame with a fill is one Stack. They replace hand-written flex/grid CSS so spacing always comes from the Figma scale.
use: Stacking sections, fields or cards (Stack, gap md–lg).
Toolbars and button rows (Stack direction="row", align center, justify between).
Card and tile grids that reflow (Grid minColumnWidth) or form columns (Grid columns={{ mobile: 1, desktop: 2 }}).
Wells and plain panels (Box surface + padding).
A panel that lays out its content, Figma's auto layout frame with a fill: one Stack (or Grid) with surface, padding, gap and radius.
Page content width with the breakpoint margin (Container).
avoid: A clickable or selectable tile → Card.
Rows of data → List/ListItem or Table.
A modal or sheet surface → Dialog, SidePanel, BottomSheet.
Separating groups with lines → Divider.

One measure against its maximum, with or without a target (utilisation, hours this week) → GaugeChart (several measures on one maximum: RadialChart; a plain progress value: ProgressBar).
3–6 steps where each keeps part of the one before (leads to signed, applications to hires) → FunnelChart, first stage first (categories that aren't steps: BarList or BarChart).
Dashboard tiles → ChartCard (icon, description, value) next to Metric Cards.
A phone screen whose one main chart is the point → the chart straight on the screen, without a Chart Card (its padding costs the plot its width): a heading, a full-width Segmented, the chart.
avoid: One number → Metric / MetricCard.
Exact values to compare or export → Table.
More than ~7 series or slices → split the chart or use a Table.
A donut for values over time → LineChart or BarChart.
One progress value with a label → ProgressBar / ProgressCircle, not a RadialChart.
Values over time, or more than 8 items, in a BarList → BarChart or a Table.
Values without a target in a BulletChart → BarList or BarChart.
A gauge for values over time or for several measures → LineChart, RadialChart or BulletChart.
A funnel for categories, or for stages that grow → BarList or BarChart.
More than 3 series in a GroupedBarChart, or stacked areas whose series aren't parts of one total → StackBarChart, LineChart or a Table.
A ComboChart for two measures in the same unit → GroupedBarChart or LineChart compare.

ChartCard.name: ChartCard
ChartCard.import: import { LineChart, BarChart, StackBarChart, DonutChart, RadialChart, HeatmapChart, BarList, BulletChart, GaugeChart, FunnelChart, AreaChart, GroupedBarChart, ComboChart, ChartCard } from "@zen-ds/react";
ChartCard.purpose: One chart family in one style: how a value changes over time (Line, Area), compares across periods or categories (Bar; 2–3 series side by side: Grouped bar), splits a total (Stack bar, Stacked area, Donut), reads two measures in different units over the same periods (Combo), measures against a maximum (Radial), ranks items (Bar list), tracks goals against their targets (Bullet), reads one measure against its maximum and target (Gauge), follows the drop-off between stages (Funnel) or spreads over two dimensions (Heatmap), framed by a Chart Card with a title, a figure and a range switch. Every chart draws itself in when it mounts and when its data changes.
use: A trend over 4–12 periods → LineChart.
Against last year, the plan or a second measure over the same periods → LineChart compare (one dashed comparison line, with a legend).
Compare periods or categories → BarChart (vertical).
Long category names or a goal per bar → BarChart orientation="horizontal" with target.
A forecast → projected bars.
Part-to-whole across periods → StackBarChart with a legend.
One measure over time where its volume matters as much as its trend (hours, sessions) → AreaChart.
2–4 parts of a total over time → AreaChart type="stacked" (the top line is the total, the legend names the bands).
2–3 measures side by side per period or category (invoiced vs. collected, this year vs. last) → GroupedBarChart with its legend.
Parts of one total → StackBarChart.
Two measures in different units over the same periods (revenue and margin %, hours and utilisation) → ComboChart: bars on the start axis, a line on the end axis.
A share on a fixed 0 – 100% axis → lineMax={100}.
Shares of one total (2–7) → DonutChart.
1–4 measures against the same maximum (budget used, goals) → RadialChart.
A value per day × hour, or any row × column grid → HeatmapChart.
A ranking of 3–8 items with their values (top clients, pages, products) → BarList, ranked largest first: the names sit in the bars, the values line up at the end.
Many rows to sort, filter or export → Table.
1–4 goals against their targets, each in its own unit (revenue, new clients, utilisation) → BulletChart.
Shares of the same maximum as rings → RadialChart.
One progress value → ProgressBar.
One measure against its maximum, with or without a target (utilisation, hours this week) → GaugeChart (several measures on one maximum: RadialChart; a plain progress value: ProgressBar).
3–6 steps where each keeps part of the one before (leads to signed, applications to hires) → FunnelChart, first stage first (categories that aren't steps: BarList or BarChart).
Dashboard tiles → ChartCard (icon, description, value) next to Metric Cards.
A phone screen whose one main chart is the point → the chart straight on the screen, without a Chart Card (its padding costs the plot its width): a heading, a full-width Segmented, the chart.
avoid: One number → Metric / MetricCard.
Exact values to compare or export → Table.
More than ~7 series or slices → split the chart or use a Table.
A donut for values over time → LineChart or BarChart.
One progress value with a label → ProgressBar / ProgressCircle, not a RadialChart.
Values over time, or more than 8 items, in a BarList → BarChart or a Table.
Values without a target in a BulletChart → BarList or BarChart.
A gauge for values over time or for several measures → LineChart, RadialChart or BulletChart.
A funnel for categories, or for stages that grow → BarList or BarChart.
More than 3 series in a GroupedBarChart, or stacked areas whose series aren't parts of one total → StackBarChart, LineChart or a Table.
A ComboChart for two measures in the same unit → GroupedBarChart or LineChart compare.

ComboChart.name: ComboChart
ComboChart.import: import { LineChart, BarChart, StackBarChart, DonutChart, RadialChart, HeatmapChart, BarList, BulletChart, GaugeChart, FunnelChart, AreaChart, GroupedBarChart, ComboChart, ChartCard } from "@zen-ds/react";
ComboChart.purpose: One chart family in one style: how a value changes over time (Line, Area), compares across periods or categories (Bar; 2–3 series side by side: Grouped bar), splits a total (Stack bar, Stacked area, Donut), reads two measures in different units over the same periods (Combo), measures against a maximum (Radial), ranks items (Bar list), tracks goals against their targets (Bullet), reads one measure against its maximum and target (Gauge), follows the drop-off between stages (Funnel) or spreads over two dimensions (Heatmap), framed by a Chart Card with a title, a figure and a range switch. Every chart draws itself in when it mounts and when its data changes.
use: A trend over 4–12 periods → LineChart.
Against last year, the plan or a second measure over the same periods → LineChart compare (one dashed comparison line, with a legend).
Compare periods or categories → BarChart (vertical).
Long category names or a goal per bar → BarChart orientation="horizontal" with target.
A forecast → projected bars.
Part-to-whole across periods → StackBarChart with a legend.
One measure over time where its volume matters as much as its trend (hours, sessions) → AreaChart.
2–4 parts of a total over time → AreaChart type="stacked" (the top line is the total, the legend names the bands).
2–3 measures side by side per period or category (invoiced vs. collected, this year vs. last) → GroupedBarChart with its legend.
Parts of one total → StackBarChart.
Two measures in different units over the same periods (revenue and margin %, hours and utilisation) → ComboChart: bars on the start axis, a line on the end axis.
A share on a fixed 0 – 100% axis → lineMax={100}.
Shares of one total (2–7) → DonutChart.
1–4 measures against the same maximum (budget used, goals) → RadialChart.
A value per day × hour, or any row × column grid → HeatmapChart.
A ranking of 3–8 items with their values (top clients, pages, products) → BarList, ranked largest first: the names sit in the bars, the values line up at the end.
Many rows to sort, filter or export → Table.
1–4 goals against their targets, each in its own unit (revenue, new clients, utilisation) → BulletChart.
Shares of the same maximum as rings → RadialChart.
One progress value → ProgressBar.
One measure against its maximum, with or without a target (utilisation, hours this week) → GaugeChart (several measures on one maximum: RadialChart; a plain progress value: ProgressBar).
3–6 steps where each keeps part of the one before (leads to signed, applications to hires) → FunnelChart, first stage first (categories that aren't steps: BarList or BarChart).
Dashboard tiles → ChartCard (icon, description, value) next to Metric Cards.
A phone screen whose one main chart is the point → the chart straight on the screen, without a Chart Card (its padding costs the plot its width): a heading, a full-width Segmented, the chart.
avoid: One number → Metric / MetricCard.
Exact values to compare or export → Table.
More than ~7 series or slices → split the chart or use a Table.
A donut for values over time → LineChart or BarChart.
One progress value with a label → ProgressBar / ProgressCircle, not a RadialChart.
Values over time, or more than 8 items, in a BarList → BarChart or a Table.
Values without a target in a BulletChart → BarList or BarChart.
A gauge for values over time or for several measures → LineChart, RadialChart or BulletChart.
A funnel for categories, or for stages that grow → BarList or BarChart.
More than 3 series in a GroupedBarChart, or stacked areas whose series aren't parts of one total → StackBarChart, LineChart or a Table.
A ComboChart for two measures in the same unit → GroupedBarChart or LineChart compare.

Container.name: Container

Stack, Grid and Box are Figma's frames: each takes the fill (background layer), stroke, corner radius, effect style, opacity, rotation and flip, so an auto layout frame with a fill is one Stack. They replace hand-written flex/grid CSS so spacing always comes from the Figma scale.
use: Stacking sections, fields or cards (Stack, gap md–lg).
Toolbars and button rows (Stack direction="row", align center, justify between).
Card and tile grids that reflow (Grid minColumnWidth) or form columns (Grid columns={{ mobile: 1, desktop: 2 }}).
Wells and plain panels (Box surface + padding).

Page content width with the breakpoint margin (Container).
avoid: A clickable or selectable tile → Card.
Rows of data → List/ListItem or Table.
A modal or sheet surface → Dialog, SidePanel, BottomSheet.
Separating groups with lines → Divider.

maxWidth.description: Content width: sm 640 (forms) · md 960 (settings, reading) · lg 1280 (dashboards, default) · xl 1440 · full (list and table pages: a page whose content is a non-widget Table spans

avoid: Data over time → LineChart.

DonutChart.name: DonutChart
DonutChart.import: import { LineChart, BarChart, StackBarChart, DonutChart, RadialChart, HeatmapChart, BarList, BulletChart, GaugeChart, FunnelChart, AreaChart, GroupedBarChart, ComboChart, ChartCard } from "@zen-ds/react";
DonutChart.purpose: One chart family in one style: how a value changes over time (Line, Area), compares across periods or categories (Bar; 2–3 series side by side: Grouped bar), splits a total (Stack bar, Stacked area, Donut), reads two measures in different units over the same periods (Combo), measures against a maximum (Radial), ranks items (Bar list), tracks goals against their targets (Bullet), reads one measure against its maximum and target (Gauge), follows the drop-off between stages (Funnel) or spreads over two dimensions (Heatmap), framed by a Chart Card with a title, a figure and a range switch. Every chart draws itself in when it mounts and when its data changes.
use: A trend over 4–12 periods → LineChart.
Against last year, the plan or a second measure over the same periods → LineChart compare (one dashed comparison line, with a legend).
Compare periods or categories → BarChart (vertical).
Long category names or a goal per bar → BarChart orientation="horizontal" with target.
A forecast → projected bars.
Part-to-whole across periods → StackBarChart with a legend.
One measure over time where its volume matters as much as its trend (hours, sessions) → AreaChart.
2–4 parts of a total over time → AreaChart type="stacked" (the top line is the total, the legend names the bands).
2–3 measures side by side per period or category (invoiced vs. collected, this year vs. last) → GroupedBarChart with its legend.
Parts of one total → StackBarChart.
Two measures in different units over the same periods (revenue and margin %, hours and utilisation) → ComboChart: bars on the start axis, a line on the end axis.
A share on a fixed 0 – 100% axis → lineMax={100}.
Shares of one total (2–7) → DonutChart.
1–4 measures against the same maximum (budget used, goals) → RadialChart.
A value per day × hour, or any row × column grid → HeatmapChart.
A ranking of 3–8 items with their values (top clients, pages, products) → BarList, ranked largest first: the names sit in the bars, the values line up at the end.
Many rows to sort, filter or export → Table.
1–4 goals against their targets, each in its own unit (revenue, new clients, utilisation) → BulletChart.
Shares of the same maximum as rings → RadialChart.
One progress value → ProgressBar.
One measure against its maximum, with or without a target (utilisation, hours this week) → GaugeChart (several measures on one maximum: RadialChart; a plain progress value: ProgressBar).
3–6 steps where each keeps part of the one before (leads to signed, applications to hires) → FunnelChart, first stage first (categories that aren't steps: BarList or BarChart).
Dashboard tiles → ChartCard (icon, description, value) next to Metric Cards.
A phone screen whose one main chart is the point → the chart straight on the screen, without a Chart Card (its padding costs the plot its width): a heading, a full-width Segmented, the chart.
avoid: One number → Metric / MetricCard.
Exact values to compare or export → Table.
More than ~7 series or slices → split the chart or use a Table.
A donut for values over time → LineChart or BarChart.
One progress value with a label → ProgressBar / ProgressCircle, not a RadialChart.
Values over time, or more than 8 items, in a BarList → BarChart or a Table.
Values without a target in a BulletChart → BarList or BarChart.
A gauge for values over time or for several measures → LineChart, RadialChart or BulletChart.
A funnel for categories, or for stages that grow → BarList or BarChart.
More than 3 series in a GroupedBarChart, or stacked areas whose series aren't parts of one total → StackBarChart, LineChart or a Table.
A ComboChart for two measures in the same unit → GroupedBarChart or LineChart compare.

FunnelChart.name: FunnelChart
FunnelChart.import: import { LineChart, BarChart, StackBarChart, DonutChart, RadialChart, HeatmapChart, BarList, BulletChart, GaugeChart, FunnelChart, AreaChart, GroupedBarChart, ComboChart, ChartCard } from "@zen-ds/react";
FunnelChart.purpose: One chart family in one style: how a value changes over time (Line, Area), compares across periods or categories (Bar; 2–3 series side by side: Grouped bar), splits a total (Stack bar, Stacked area, Donut), reads two measures in different units over the same periods (Combo), measures against a maximum (Radial), ranks items (Bar list), tracks goals against their targets (Bullet), reads one measure against its maximum and target (Gauge), follows the drop-off between stages (Funnel) or spreads over two dimensions (Heatmap), framed by a Chart Card with a title, a figure and a range switch. Every chart draws itself in when it mounts and when its data changes.
use: A trend over 4–12 periods → LineChart.
Against last year, the plan or a second measure over the same periods → LineChart compare (one dashed comparison line, with a legend).
Compare periods or categories → BarChart (vertical).
Long category names or a goal per bar → BarChart orientation="horizontal" with target.
A forecast → projected bars.
Part-to-whole across periods → StackBarChart with a legend.
One measure over time where its volume matters as much as its trend (hours, sessions) → AreaChart.
2–4 parts of a total over time → AreaChart type="stacked" (the top line is the total, the legend names the bands).
2–3 measures side by side per period or category (invoiced vs. collected, this year vs. last) → GroupedBarChart with its legend.
Parts of one total → StackBarChart.
Two measures in different units over the same periods (revenue and margin %, hours and utilisation) → ComboChart: bars on the start axis, a line on the end axis.
A share on a fixed 0 – 100% axis → lineMax={100}.
Shares of one total (2–7) → DonutChart.
1–4 measures against the same maximum (budget used, goals) → RadialChart.
A value per day × hour, or any row × column grid → HeatmapChart.
A ranking of 3–8 items with their values (top clients, pages, products) → BarList, ranked largest first: the names sit in the bars, the values line up at the end.
Many rows to sort, filter or export → Table.
1–4 goals against their targets, each in its own unit (revenue, new clients, utilisation) → BulletChart.
Shares of the same maximum as rings → RadialChart.
One progress value → ProgressBar.
One measure against its maximum, with or without a target (utilisation, hours this week) → GaugeChart (several measures on one maximum: RadialChart; a plain progress value: ProgressBar).
3–6 steps where each keeps part of the one before (leads to signed, applications to hires) → FunnelChart, first stage first (categories that aren't steps: BarList or BarChart).
Dashboard tiles → ChartCard (icon, description, value) next to Metric Cards.
A phone screen whose one main chart is the point → the chart straight on the screen, without a Chart Card (its padding costs the plot its width): a heading, a full-width Segmented, the chart.
avoid: One number → Metric / MetricCard.
Exact values to compare or export → Table.
More than ~7 series or slices → split the chart or use a Table.
A donut for values over time → LineChart or BarChart.
One progress value with a label → ProgressBar / ProgressCircle, not a RadialChart.
Values over time, or more than 8 items, in a BarList → BarChart or a Table.
Values without a target in a BulletChart → BarList or BarChart.
A gauge for values over time or for several measures → LineChart, RadialChart or BulletChart.
A funnel for categories, or for stages that grow → BarList or BarChart.
More than 3 series in a GroupedBarChart, or stacked areas whose series aren't parts of one total → StackBarChart, LineChart or a Table.
A ComboChart for two measures in the same unit → GroupedBarChart or LineChart compare.

Grid.import: import { Stack, Grid, Box, Container } from "@zen-ds/react";
Grid.purpose: Token-based layout primitives: Stack (one direction), Grid (columns), Box (a frame without auto layout) and Container (page width and margin). Stack, Grid and Box are Figma's frames: each takes the fill (background layer), stroke, corner radius, effect style, opacity, rotation and flip, so an auto layout frame with a fill is one Stack. They replace hand-written flex/grid CSS so spacing always comes from the Figma scale.
use: Stacking sections, fields or cards (Stack, gap md–lg).
Toolbars and button rows (Stack direction="row", align center, justify between).
Card and tile grids that reflow (Grid minColumnWidth) or form columns (Grid columns={{ mobile: 1, desktop: 2 }}).
Wells and plain panels (Box surface + padding).
A panel that lays out its content, Figma's auto layout frame with a fill: one Stack (or Grid) with surface, padding, gap and radius.
Page content width with the breakpoint margin (Container).
avoid: A clickable or selectable tile → Card.
Rows of data → List/ListItem or Table.
A modal or sheet surface → Dialog, SidePanel, BottomSheet.
Separating groups with lines → Divider.

HeatmapChart.import: import { LineChart, BarChart, StackBarChart, DonutChart, RadialChart, HeatmapChart, BarList, BulletChart, GaugeChart, FunnelChart, AreaChart, GroupedBarChart, ComboChart, ChartCard } from "@zen-ds/react";
HeatmapChart.purpose: One chart family in one style: how a value changes over time (Line, Area), compares across periods or categories (Bar; 2–3 series side by side: Grouped bar), splits a total (Stack bar, Stacked area, Donut), reads two measures in different units over the same periods (Combo), measures against a maximum (Radial), ranks items (Bar list), tracks goals against their targets (Bullet), reads one measure against its maximum and target (Gauge), follows the drop-off between stages (Funnel) or spreads over two dimensions (Heatmap), framed by a Chart Card with a title, a figure and a range switch. Every chart draws itself in when it mounts and when its data changes.
use: A trend over 4–12 periods → LineChart.
Against last year, the plan or a second measure over the same periods → LineChart compare (one dashed comparison line, with a legend).
Compare periods or categories → BarChart (vertical).
Long category names or a goal per bar → BarChart orientation="horizontal" with target.
A forecast → projected bars.
Part-to-whole across periods → StackBarChart with a legend.
One measure over time where its volume matters as much as its trend (hours, sessions) → AreaChart.
2–4 parts of a total over time → AreaChart type="stacked" (the top line is the total, the legend names the bands).
2–3 measures side by side per period or category (invoiced vs. collected, this year vs. last) → GroupedBarChart with its legend.
Parts of one total → StackBarChart.
Two measures in different units over the same periods (revenue and margin %, hours and utilisation) → ComboChart: bars on the start axis, a line on the end axis.
A share on a fixed 0 – 100% axis → lineMax={100}.
Shares of one total (2–7) → DonutChart.
1–4 measures against the same maximum (budget used, goals) → RadialChart.
A value per day × hour, or any row × column grid → HeatmapChart.
A ranking of 3–8 items with their values (top clients, pages, products) → BarList, ranked largest first: the names sit in the bars, the values line up at the end.
Many rows to sort, filter or export → Table.
1–4 goals against their targets, each in its own unit (revenue, new clients, utilisation) → BulletChart.
Shares of the same maximum as rings → RadialChart.
One progress value → ProgressBar.
One measure against its maximum, with or without a target (utilisation, hours this week) → GaugeChart (several measures on one maximum: RadialChart; a plain progress value: ProgressBar).
3–6 steps where each keeps part of the one before (leads to signed, applications to hires) → FunnelChart, first stage first (categories that aren't steps: BarList or BarChart).
Dashboard tiles → ChartCard (icon, description, value) next to Metric Cards.
A phone screen whose one main chart is the point → the chart straight on the screen, without a Chart Card (its padding costs the plot its width): a heading, a full-width Segmented, the chart.
avoid: One number → Metric / MetricCard.
Exact values to compare or export → Table.
More than ~7 series or slices → split the chart or use a Table.
A donut for values over time → LineChart or BarChart.
One progress value with a label → ProgressBar / ProgressCircle, not a RadialChart.
Values over time, or more than 8 items, in a BarList → BarChart or a Table.
Values without a target in a BulletChart → BarList or BarChart.
A gauge for values over time or for several measures → LineChart, RadialChart or BulletChart.
A funnel for categories, or for stages that grow → BarList or BarChart.
More than 3 series in a GroupedBarChart, or stacked areas whose series aren't parts of one total → StackBarChart, LineChart or a Table.
A ComboChart for two measures in the same unit → GroupedBarChart or LineChart compare.

InputField.purpose: Collect a single value from the user. All fields share Label → Field → Help-Text anatomy and the Leading/Trailing slots.

Long text → TextAreaField.

One option from a list → SelectField (≤ 10 options), otherwise AutocompleteField. On mobile (breakpoint mobile, or inside a phone frame) SelectField opens its options in a Bottom Sheet — a List with the picked row selected and checked; a pick closes it — instead of the Popover.
Dates → DateField.
Any colour → ColorField (it opens ColorPicker).

Quantities → NumberField (steppers).
Inline editable titles → HeadingField: one line for short names (a board, a file), multiline when titles run long (documents, announcements, tasks).
Formatted long text (announcements, descriptions) → RichTextField.

A record's properties edited in place — status, priority, dates, people, labels on a task, ticket or deal → PropertyField with one value cell (PropertyText, PropertySelect, PropertyStatus, PropertyDate, PropertyPeople, PropertyTags): the label column on the left, the borderless value on the right, rows Spacing/Gap/2XSmall apart.

RadialChart.name: RadialChart
RadialChart.import: import { LineChart, BarChart, StackBarChart, DonutChart, RadialChart, HeatmapChart, BarList, BulletChart, GaugeChart, FunnelChart, AreaChart, GroupedBarChart, ComboChart, ChartCard } from "@zen-ds/react";
RadialChart.purpose: One chart family in one style: how a value changes over time (Line, Area), compares across periods or categories (Bar; 2–3 series side by side: Grouped bar), splits a total (Stack bar, Stacked area, Donut), reads two measures in different units over the same periods (Combo), measures against a maximum (Radial), ranks items (Bar list), tracks goals against their targets (Bullet), reads one measure against its maximum and target (Gauge), follows the drop-off between stages (Funnel) or spreads over two dimensions (Heatmap), framed by a Chart Card with a title, a figure and a range switch. Every chart draws itself in when it mounts and when its data changes.
use: A trend over 4–12 periods → LineChart.
Against last year, the plan or a second measure over the same periods → LineChart compare (one dashed comparison line, with a legend).
Compare periods or categories → BarChart (vertical).
Long category names or a goal per bar → BarChart orientation="horizontal" with target.
A forecast → projected bars.
Part-to-whole across periods → StackBarChart with a legend.
One measure over time where its volume matters as much as its trend (hours, sessions) → AreaChart.
2–4 parts of a total over time → AreaChart type="stacked" (the top line is the total, the legend names the bands).
2–3 measures side by side per period or category (invoiced vs. collected, this year vs. last) → GroupedBarChart with its legend.
Parts of one total → StackBarChart.
Two measures in different units over the same periods (revenue and margin %, hours and utilisation) → ComboChart: bars on the start axis, a line on the end axis.
A share on a fixed 0 – 100% axis → lineMax={100}.
Shares of one total (2–7) → DonutChart.
1–4 measures against the same maximum (budget used, goals) → RadialChart.
A value per day × hour, or any row × column grid → HeatmapChart.
A ranking of 3–8 items with their values (top clients, pages, products) → BarList, ranked largest first: the names sit in the bars, the values line up at the end.
Many rows to sort, filter or export → Table.
1–4 goals against their targets, each in its own unit (revenue, new clients, utilisation) → BulletChart.
Shares of the same maximum as rings → RadialChart.
One progress value → ProgressBar.
One measure against its maximum, with or without a target (utilisation, hours this week) → GaugeChart (several measures on one maximum: RadialChart; a plain progress value: ProgressBar).
3–6 steps where each keeps part of the one before (leads to signed, applications to hires) → FunnelChart, first stage first (categories that aren't steps: BarList or BarChart).
Dashboard tiles → ChartCard (icon, description, value) next to Metric Cards.
A phone screen whose one main chart is the point → the chart straight on the screen, without a Chart Card (its padding costs the plot its width): a heading, a full-width Segmented, the chart.
avoid: One number → Metric / MetricCard.
Exact values to compare or export → Table.
More than ~7 series or slices → split the chart or use a Table.
A donut for values over time → LineChart or BarChart.
One progress value with a label → ProgressBar / ProgressCircle, not a RadialChart.
Values over time, or more than 8 items, in a BarList → BarChart or a Table.
Values without a target in a BulletChart → BarList or BarChart.
A gauge for values over time or for several measures → LineChart, RadialChart or BulletChart.
A funnel for categories, or for stages that grow → BarList or BarChart.
More than 3 series in a GroupedBarChart, or stacked areas whose series aren't parts of one total → StackBarChart, LineChart or a Table.
A ComboChart for two measures in the same unit → GroupedBarChart or LineChart compare.

SelectField.name: SelectField
SelectField.import: import { InputField, SelectField, DateField, ColorField, NumberField, TextAreaField, AutocompleteField, RichTextField, PropertyField, PropertyText, PropertySelect, PropertyStatus, PropertyDate, PropertyPeople, PropertyTags, InputLabel, InputHelpText, InputLeadingTrailing, InputContent, ControlBarSelectItem, RichTextEditorBar, HeadingField, InputConditionItem, InputConditions } from "@zen-ds/react";
SelectField.purpose: Collect a single value from the user. All fields share Label → Field → Help-Text anatomy and the Leading/Trailing slots.
use: Free text → InputField.
Long text → TextAreaField.

One option from a list → SelectField (≤ 10 options), otherwise AutocompleteField. On mobile (breakpoint mobile, or inside a phone frame) SelectField opens its options in a Bottom Sheet — a List with the picked row selected and checked; a pick closes it — instead of the Popover.
Dates → DateField.
Any colour → ColorField (it opens ColorPicker).

Dense property panels and inspectors → layout="inline" on InputField, SelectField or ColorField (Figma Input/Inline-Field): the label inside the field, the value at the end, rows Spacing/Gap/XSmall apart.
Quantities → NumberField (steppers).
Inline editable titles → HeadingField: one line for short names (a board, a file), multiline when titles run long (documents, announcements, tasks).
Formatted long text (announcements, descriptions) → RichTextField.

A record's properties edited in place — status, priority, dates, people, labels on a task, ticket or deal → PropertyField with one value cell (PropertyText, PropertySelect, PropertyStatus, PropertyDate, PropertyPeople, PropertyTags): the label column on the left, the borderless value on the right, rows Spacing/Gap/2XSmall apart.
avoid: Searching/filtering content → Search.
Binary settings → Toggle or Checkbox.
2–5 mutually exclusive visible options → RadioButton group or Segmented.

Shape.name: Shape
Shape.purpose: Figma's native shapes in code — Rectangle, Ellipse with its arc (pie, ring, ring segment), Line, Arrow, Polygon, Star and the Pen's Vector — for illustrations, marks and decoration drawn in Zen Studio, coloured with Zen tokens only.
use: A decorative mark or illustration a designer drew in Zen Studio with R, O, L, ⇧L, Polygon or Star.
A free-form curve or outline drawn with the Pen (P) or Pencil (⇧P): type="vector" with its path d in its viewBox.
A cut-out or combined mark (a ticket stub, a ring with a notch): a boolean group of shapes (⌥⇧U / ⌥⇧S / ⌥⇧I / ⌥⇧E in Zen Studio).
A ring or pie built from an ellipse's arc (Start, Sweep, Ratio) where no chart component fits.
A layer at Figma's X / Y in a free frame (a Box or Screen without auto layout): position="absolute" with px insets.
A picture placed in Zen Studio (⇧⌘K, a dropped or pasted file): a Rectangle with an image fill, as Figma places it.

A divider line → Divider.
A surface or card background → Box surface or Card.
A status dot or badge on a component → that component's own prop (Avatar status, notification dot).
An icon → Icon (the icon set); a vector is drawn art, not a glyph.

Stack.purpose: Token-based layout primitives: Stack (one direction), Grid (columns), Box (a frame without auto layout) and Container (page width and margin). Stack, Grid and Box are Figma's frames: each takes the fill (background layer), stroke, corner radius, effect style, opacity, rotation and flip, so an auto layout frame with a fill is one Stack. They replace hand-written flex/grid CSS so spacing always comes from the Figma scale.

Toolbars and button rows (Stack direction="row", align center, justify between).

Page content width with the breakpoint margin (Container).
avoid: A clickable or selectable tile → Card.
Rows of data → List/ListItem or Table.
A modal or sheet surface → Dialog, SidePanel, BottomSheet.
Separating groups with lines → Divider.

StackBarChart.name: StackBarChart
StackBarChart.import: import { LineChart, BarChart, StackBarChart, DonutChart, RadialChart, HeatmapChart, BarList, BulletChart, GaugeChart, FunnelChart, AreaChart, GroupedBarChart, ComboChart, ChartCard } from "@zen-ds/react";
StackBarChart.purpose: One chart family in one style: how a value changes over time (Line, Area), compares across periods or categories (Bar; 2–3 series side by side: Grouped bar), splits a total (Stack bar, Stacked area, Donut), reads two measures in different units over the same periods (Combo), measures against a maximum (Radial), ranks items (Bar list), tracks goals against their targets (Bullet), reads one measure against its maximum and target (Gauge), follows the drop-off between stages (Funnel) or spreads over two dimensions (Heatmap), framed by a Chart Card with a title, a figure and a range switch. Every chart draws itself in when it mounts and when its data changes.
use: A trend over 4–12 periods → LineChart.
Against last year, the plan or a second measure over the same periods → LineChart compare (one dashed comparison line, with a legend).
Compare periods or categories → BarChart (vertical).
Long category names or a goal per bar → BarChart orientation="horizontal" with target.
A forecast → projected bars.
Part-to-whole across periods → StackBarChart with a legend.
One measure over time where its volume matters as much as its trend (hours, sessions) → AreaChart.
2–4 parts of a total over time → AreaChart type="stacked" (the top line is the total, the legend names the bands).
2–3 measures side by side per period or category (invoiced vs. collected, this year vs. last) → GroupedBarChart with its legend.
Parts of one total → StackBarChart.
Two measures in different units over the same periods (revenue and margin %, hours and utilisation) → ComboChart: bars on the start axis, a line on the end axis.
A share on a fixed 0 – 100% axis → lineMax={100}.
Shares of one total (2–7) → DonutChart.
1–4 measures against the same maximum (budget used, goals) → RadialChart.
A value per day × hour, or any row × column grid → HeatmapChart.
A ranking of 3–8 items with their values (top clients, pages, products) → BarList, ranked largest first: the names sit in the bars, the values line up at the end.
Many rows to sort, filter or export → Table.
1–4 goals against their targets, each in its own unit (revenue, new clients, utilisation) → BulletChart.
Shares of the same maximum as rings → RadialChart.
One progress value → ProgressBar.
One measure against its maximum, with or without a target (utilisation, hours this week) → GaugeChart (several measures on one maximum: RadialChart; a plain progress value: ProgressBar).
3–6 steps where each keeps part of the one before (leads to signed, applications to hires) → FunnelChart, first stage first (categories that aren't steps: BarList or BarChart).
Dashboard tiles → ChartCard (icon, description, value) next to Metric Cards.
A phone screen whose one main chart is the point → the chart straight on the screen, without a Chart Card (its padding costs the plot its width): a heading, a full-width Segmented, the chart.
avoid: One number → Metric / MetricCard.
Exact values to compare or export → Table.
More than ~7 series or slices → split the chart or use a Table.
A donut for values over time → LineChart or BarChart.
One progress value with a label → ProgressBar / ProgressCircle, not a RadialChart.
Values over time, or more than 8 items, in a BarList → BarChart or a Table.
Values without a target in a BulletChart → BarList or BarChart.
A gauge for values over time or for several measures → LineChart, RadialChart or BulletChart.
A funnel for categories, or for stages that grow → BarList or BarChart.
More than 3 series in a GroupedBarChart, or stacked areas whose series aren't parts of one total → StackBarChart, LineChart or a Table.
A ComboChart for two measures in the same unit → GroupedBarChart or LineChart compare.

button.title: Button & IconButton
do: Give each surface exactly one Primary button, the main CTA.
Use Tertiary for every other action; it is the most common level.
Pair actions as Tertiary (dismiss) + Primary (commit), with Primary last, on the right.
Use Danger or Danger-Subtle for irreversible actions (Delete, Discard).
Start labels with a verb and keep them to 1–3 words ("Save changes", "Invite").
Disable a button only while its precondition is unmet, and explain why nearby (help text, validation).
Show progress on the button itself ("Deleting…") and disable siblings while it runs.
Use Flat Primary (Button/Icon-Flat Small) for close and dismiss icon buttons in Dialog, ModalForm and Side Panel headers (harness: button/flat-level).
Size buttons by layout: a full-width button (mobile CTA, empty state, stacked form footer) is Medium or larger; Small buttons (2xs · xs · sm) hug their label and align to the start.

On a phone, put the main action in the footer as Large (lg) full-width buttons, Primary on top and at most one Tertiary alternative below; small sizes (2xs–sm) always hug their label (harness: button/small-full-width).

Let every icon-only action show its name as a tooltip after 1s of hover (IconButton does it by default; custom icon-only controls spread useIconTooltip(label).bind() and render .tooltip) (harness: icon-button/tooltip, button/icon-only-raw).
dont: Don't use Secondary as the default second button. It is a rare highlight (e.g. a pressed toolbar toggle); justify it with zen-allow-secondary.
Don't use Accent for ordinary primaries; reserve it for promoted CTAs (upsell, onboarding, the floating feedback action).
Don't put two Primary buttons side by side.
Don't use a Button to open a filter/sort list.
Don't ship an IconButton without aria-label.
Don't use vague labels ("OK", "Click here") for consequential actions.
Don't use "OK", "Yes", "Submit" or "Click here"; name the outcome (harness: button/vague-label).

Don't stretch a Small button (2xs · xs · sm) across its container: a thin, wide button reads as a divider or input, and the label floats in empty space. Use size md, or let it hug (harness: button/small-full-width).
Don't label a Button "Filters" or give it a filter icon to open filters; that trigger is a Chip (harness: button/filter-is-chip).
Don't draw a Back button or IconButton with a left arrow on mobile/tablet; use icon-chevron-left-line-medium (harness: navigation/back-chevron).
Don't build an icon-only action from a raw <button> + <Icon>, and don't pass tooltip={false} unless a visible label sits right beside it.

Don't use XSmall / 2XSmall text buttons for ordinary actions (examples, cards, toolbars, forms, footers) — use sm or larger. XSmall/2XSmall are only for special compact pills beside a row, like the App Store's Get · Install · Open (harness: button/compact-size-special).

chip.title: Chip / Pill
do: On a colour band, a Solid hue card or a photo, give every chip an overlay level (ChipGroup too): black-overlay by default (level="overlay"), white-overlay on a solid colour. Primary and Secondary take mode tokens that flip in dark mode, and their Accent focus ring vanishes on the band.
When exactly one value applies (Repeat: Daily / Weekly / Monthly), use <ChipGroup>: it is a radio group with roving focus and aria-checked; never hand-set role="radio" on Chips.

Pick the level by how many can be on (user rule 2026-10-04): a multi-select group of toggles is Secondary for every chip (Selected = the 2px dark outline), a single-select group is Primary for every chip (Selected = the dark fill). Never switch a chip's level when it is selected.
Put a group of chips in its own Stack (or chip row) with Spacing/Gap/XSmall (8px) between chips, never the gap of the form or fieldset around it.
Keep the medium size (the default) on desktop and phones, so a filter row lines up with Search and Buttons (40px); small only inside a genuinely narrow component space.
Use one Advanced chip per filter dimension (Status, Owner, Date).
Show a count with a Number-only chip and no handler: it renders as a static count (Figma: a compact indicator for counts). Give it onClick or selected only when pressing the number does something.
Show the chosen value as the chip label for single selection; show the counter for multiple.
Wire onClearSelection so Delete/Backspace and the × clear the filter.
Offer "Clear all" (Tertiary button) when two or more filters are active.
Keep Advanced chips' Popover open while toggling multiple options (popoverMultiple).
Show the count on multiple-selection chips (harness: chip/multiple-needs-count).

On a phone, keep filter chips in one horizontally scrolling row (no wrapping) and open choices in a Bottom Sheet of List + ListItem rows (the picked one `selected`) instead of a Popover; show the result count with a plural label and offer Clear filters on an empty result.
dont: Don't use Secondary or any Button to open a filter list.
Don't use an overlay level on a page surface (Canvas, Surface, a Pale card), and don't put white-overlay on a light colour or photo: its light text needs a dark or saturated colour under it.

In a row that scrolls sideways on a wider screen (overflow-x: auto clips both axes), pass `popoverPortal` so the chip's menu opens in the overlay layer, whole and anchored under it; leave it off inside a Dialog or Bottom Sheet.
Don't use Segmented to filter data (Segmented switches views).
Don't give a Normal or Number-only chip popoverItems.
Don't wrap chips inside another button.

input.title: Input fields
do: Always render a visible label; use aria-label only when the context already labels the field (e.g. a Share link row).
Validate on blur or submit, then show error text that says how to fix it.
Use Read-only for values the user may see but not change.
Read-only fields stay focusable (to read, select and copy) and show the Focused 3px ring around the dashed Read-Only border, whose dashes take Color/Focus/Neutral/Solid while focused.
Use Disabled for a field that is unavailable until something else changes (a toggle, a plan, a permission), and say why in the help text.
Use helpTheme="warning" for a soft caution and "positive" to confirm a check passed; reserve Negative for `error`.

Make a labelled Leading/Trailing slot a picker (options) for units, country codes or account types, or an action (onClick) such as show password; set interactive={false} when it is purely informative.

Escape closes only an open SelectField list, DateField calendar, Leading/Trailing picker or AutocompleteField list and returns focus to its trigger; a Dialog, ModalForm or Side Panel around the field stays open. On a closed field, Escape goes to that overlay.

DateField opens its calendar when a person tabs to or clicks the field, never on a script's focus (a blocked submit's focusFirstInvalidField, a Dialog's or BottomSheet's first focus), so an error focus never covers the form with the calendar.

A typed date outside minDate / maxDate stays in the DateField, reaches onValueChange and marks the input aria-invalid (Form and ModalForm count it and focus it after a blocked submit), but the field shows no message of its own: validate it and pass `error` that names the allowed range ("Pick a date from 1 October").
AutocompleteField: with onCreate, Create appears only for a value that is not an option yet; typing an option that is already a Tag lists it as selected (disabled) instead.
Clamp NumberField with min/max; steppers disable at the bounds.
Keep help text to one line; move long guidance to InputConditions or docs.
Show requirement rules (passwords, handles) as InputConditions under the field: Default before typing, then Success/Wrong live as the value changes.
RichTextField: read content through onValueChange(html, text), store the HTML and render it through your sanitizer.
RichTextField: keep the Control-Bar (editorBar) unless the surface is tiny.

RichTextField keeps its own undo history: Undo / Redo (⌘Z, ⇧⌘Z, Ctrl+Y) step through this field's edits only and are disabled while there is nothing to undo or redo; replacing `value` from outside (clearing after Post) starts a new history.
HeadingField: set multiline when a title can run past one line, so it wraps instead of scrolling out of view.

PropertyField: one value cell per row (harness: property-field/one-value), one label column for the whole list, two columns Spacing/Gap/XLarge apart; an empty value says the locale's "Empty"; give a select option's icon a tone by meaning (Urgent Negative, High Warning, Normal Info, Low Neutral).
PropertyField: pass readOnly for people who may not change the record, so nothing looks clickable.
dont: Don't disable a field whose value people need to read or copy; use Read-only (disabled text is faint, skipped by Tab and not submitted).
Don't use Disabled on AutocompleteField or RichTextField: Figma gives them Read-only only (harness: input/no-disabled).
Don't use placeholder text as the label.
Don't show an error before the user has interacted with the field.
Don't make an icon-only Leading/Trailing slot clickable without an aria-label; decorative slots pass clicks to the field.
Don't open a Date/Select popover on a read-only or disabled field.
Don't repeat the label as placeholder; show an example or the format (harness: input/placeholder-not-label).
Don't use RichTextField for plain notes (→ TextAreaField) or single-line input (→ InputField).
Don't wire onChange on RichTextField; it reports content through onValueChange (harness: richtext/value-not-onchange).
Don't put a bordered InputField or SelectField in a PropertyField: the borderless value cell is the field.

search.title: Search
do: Describe the scope in the placeholder ("Search components").

On phone screens prefer shape="rounded" (a pill, Figma Shape=Rounded); a Search in a TopNavigation control bar, a BottomSheet or an AppShell on a phone is rounded by default (set shape="default" to keep the square field). Desktop toolbars keep the default shape.
Filter live and show an empty state that echoes the query.
Let Enter open the first result; the clear button resets to recent items.
Pair Search with Chip filters in table toolbars. Search fills its container, so give it a Grid column: columns={{ mobile: 1, desktop: "minmax(0, 320px) 1fr" }} with the chips in the second cell.
Debounce remote search (~250ms) and keep the query when results refresh.
Show the result count in an aria-live region ("12 results").
When the filter opens a Bottom Sheet, panel or Popover, pass filterHasPopup ("dialog", "menu", "listbox") and filterExpanded={open}; aria-expanded on Search itself lands on the input.
When nothing matches, show an EmptyState that echoes the query and offers “Clear search” (size="sm" in narrow panels such as sidebars and pickers).
dont: Don't hide search behind an icon on desktop when search is a primary task.
Don't clear the query when results update.

Don't disable Search because there is nothing to find yet; keep it with an empty state, or hide it where search never applies. Disable it only while something blocks searching (a bulk edit, a sync), and say why.
Don't trigger search only on Enter for small, local lists; filter as the user types.
Don't use a vague placeholder ("Type here…").

segmented.title: Segmented
do: Use size medium (the default) on desktop and on phones; small only inside a genuinely narrow component space (a dense card header or table toolbar), never just to save room on a page.
Keep the default level (Secondary), the most common case; set level="primary" only when the switch needs extra emphasis (e.g. a billing-period toggle).

On a colour band, a Solid hue card or a photo, set an overlay level: black-overlay by default (level="overlay"), white-overlay on a solid colour. Secondary and Primary take mode tokens that flip in dark mode, and their Accent focus ring vanishes on the band.
Name the control with aria-label.
Keep labels to one or two words; icon-only items still need a label for assistive tech.
Use badges for counts and hide them at zero.
Keep the selected segment static: no hover and a default cursor, because one option is always selected and re-clicking it does nothing.
Keep 2–5 options (harness: segmented/option-count; options computed at run time are counted on the rendered page by the platform audit, kind counts). Past five, pick with a SelectField.
Name icon-only segments with "aria-label" on the option and mark the icon decorative (harness: segmented/icon-only-needs-name).

On mobile, stretch a Segmented to its container (fullWidth) in a Top Navigation control bar, a Bottom Sheet or a narrow panel, so the items share the width equally (harness: segmented/control-bar-full-width).

On a phone, use a Segmented only when every label fits its equal share (fullWidth). When the options are wider than the screen (four periods, long labels), switch to a single-choice row of Normal Chips (Medium, the pressed one Primary) that scrolls sideways, not a sliding Segmented.
dont: Don't use Segmented as a filter.

Don't use an overlay level on a page surface (Canvas, Surface, a Pale card), and don't put white-overlay on a dark colour or photo: its dark labels need a bright, saturated colour under it (black-overlay goes on dark colours and photos).
Don't abbreviate labels or shrink the text to squeeze a Segmented onto a phone, and don't let it slide sideways there; use a Chip row instead (or Tabs / SelectField past 5 options).
Don't mix icon-only and labelled items in one control.
Don't add a hover or pressed state to the selected segment; it suggests the choice can be undone by clicking it again.

toggle.title: Toggle
do: Apply the change immediately; no confirm button.
On phones use size large: components keep their full size on mobile, the smaller sizes are for dense desktop rows, tables and panels (harness: mobile/full-size-controls).
Use size xlarge for the one setting that leads a screen (Do not disturb, Location sharing), with an icon that names the setting; a list of settings stays large.
Use a master toggle to disable dependent toggles, and explain in its caption.
Label the setting, not the state ("Email notifications", not "On").
dont: Don't use a Toggle inside a form that is submitted later.
Don't add a forced hover state; real hover is built in.
Don't label a toggle with its state ("On", "Enabled") (harness: toggle/label-names-setting).
Don't use a Toggle for a one-off action ("Export now") → Button.

checkbox.title: Checkbox
do: Always give a label; clicking the label toggles.
Use indeterminate only for a parent whose children are partially selected; clicking resolves it.
Explain disabled options in the caption ("Unavailable on the Free plan").
dont: Don't use a checkbox for an action that happens immediately.
Don't pre-check consent boxes for marketing.
Don't use a Checkbox group for mutually exclusive options → RadioButton.
Don't word labels negatively ("Don't send emails"); checked should mean "yes".

radio-button.title: Radio Button
do: Wrap radios in role=radiogroup with an aria-label, and share one name.
Pre-select the recommended option when there is a safe default.
Use captions for price or consequence.
dont: Don't render a lone radio; it cannot be unselected.
Don't use radios for independent choices.
Don't use more than ~7 radios; switch to a SelectField.
Don't trigger navigation or an action on selection; radios only choose.

badge.title: Badge, Badge-Counter & Badge-Status
do: Map status to semantic themes consistently (green = success, red = failure, yellow = attention).
Use Subtle backgrounds in dense tables and Solid for emphasis.
Cap counters at "99+" and hide them at zero.

Show counts (unread, items, filters applied, a section's or folder's item count) with BadgeCounter (Figma Badge-Counter) — a round pill whose min width equals its height — never a Badge holding a number nor bare text beside a label; keep Badge for words and statuses (harness: badge/count-uses-counter, badge/count-text-uses-counter; component-usage-rules §18).
Make counts agree with their noun — "1 file" / "3 files" — with a plural helper; never print {list.length} straight before a noun (harness: copy/plural-count).

Show a workflow step with BadgeStatus, never a Badge themed by hand: the step sets the colour and the ring, so every screen reads one workflow the same way (harness: badge/workflow-status-uses-badge-status).
Keep one workflow per product, in order: To Do → In Progress → In Review → Done; Blocked and Cancelled sit outside it. Rename a step only by its label (children), never by repainting another step.
Pass progress only when you know the exact share of the work done (a project at 60%); otherwise the step's own ring says enough.
dont: Don't make a badge clickable (use Chip).
Don't make a BadgeStatus removable or clickable: a status changes in its picker (a Popover of BadgeStatus items, Input/Property-Field Type=Status).
Don't rely on colour alone; keep the text.
Don't use more than two badges on one row item; summarise the rest.
Don't show counters at zero.

tag.title: Tag
do: Let Backspace in an empty field remove the last tag.
Flag invalid values with error and explain in the field's error text.
Keep tag labels short (≤ 24 characters) and truncate with a tooltip beyond that.
dont: Don't use a Tag as a generic action button (Save, Delete) — onClick is only for acting on the value itself (filter by it, open it).
Don't use Tags for statuses (→ Badge) or filters (→ Chip).
Don't let users add duplicate values; merge them silently.

avatar.title: Avatar & Avatar Stack
do: Set alt to the person's name; use alt="" only when the name is shown next to the avatar.
Use 2 initials (1 on xsmall/2xsmall).
Use square avatars for workspaces and organisations.
Popover items (Theme=Avatar Small) use Avatar Size=Small (32px); Avatar Big uses Medium (40px) — PopoverItem sizes them for you.
dont: Don't show more than 5 avatars in a stack; summarise the rest in text.
Don't use status without a text equivalent nearby ("Online").

Don't put initials on a Solid green, teal, orange or cyan avatar: the white initials measure 2.6–2.9:1. Use background="subtle" or a theme such as indigo, violet or purple; photos are fine (harness: avatar/solid-initials-contrast).

popover.title: Popover
do: Pass `open`: a Popover is closed by default. Controlled `open={isOpen}` goes with `onOpenChange` (harness: popover/explicit-open, popover/controlled-close).
Pass images via photoSrc; the item renders the Figma size for its theme.
Avatar items are 32px (Avatar Small) or 40px (Avatar Big); long labels and captions stay on one line and end in "…".
Give it anchorRef + onOpenChange so outside-click and Escape close it and focus returns.

Keep one popover open at a time: opening a popover for another object closes the open one. Popover (with onOpenChange), Chip, Select and DatePicker do this for you; a custom popup joins with useExclusivePopover(open, close, rootRef). A popover opened from inside another popover is nested and keeps its parent open.
Keep single-select popovers closing on select; keep multi-select open.

Size the list from what it opens under: suggestions under a long search bar take `width="fill"` (as wide as the bar); long values such as domains or file paths take `width="hug"` (SelectField `popoverWidth="hug"`), so each stays whole instead of ending in "…". Keep the default 240 for short options under a chip or a button.
Offer Manual-Add-New (onPopoverCreate / onCreate) when users may need a value that isn't listed, e.g. labels, tags or keywords. The Create row appears only for a new value, and Enter creates it.

Use Popover/Bulk-Action (PopoverBulkAction) for quick actions on a selection — text, a canvas element or selected rows: name it with aria-label, group actions with PopoverBulkActionGroup and 40px dividers, Button/Icon-Flat Medium only, 6 actions at most (harness: popover/bulk-action-limit). For list selections, say how many items each action affects.
dont: Don't pass your own sized / as leading for avatar/photo themes.

Don't show popovers for two different objects side by side (e.g. two filter chips' menus, or a row menu next to a Select list); an uncontrolled Popover without onOpenChange cannot be closed by the next one (harness: popover/controlled-close).
Don't put buttons or inputs (other than the Search row) inside items.
Don't dead-end a searchable list with "No results" when creating the value is allowed; use Manual-Add-New.
Don't offer Create for closed sets (statuses, roles, countries).
Don't use Bulk-Action for page-level or navigation actions — that is a Toolbar or Sidebar.

sidebar.title: Sidebar
do: One elevation per screen, set by the Sidebar: Canvas default (grey) + the default Sidebar (Surface + shadow) + Shadow cards with no border; Canvas alt (white) + a Surface-alt or Flat Sidebar (add divider for a full-height line inside the Sidebar) + bordered cards; Canvas flat + a Flat Sidebar + bordered cards. Never a shadowed Sidebar on a white Canvas.
Give destinations an href so rows are real links (open in a new tab, copy the address), and pass the current route's id as selectedId instead of remapping selected in sections.
Put footer destinations (Settings, Help) in footer as <SidebarMenuItem> rows, as Figma's Footer-Content holds Menu-Items: the same row, selection and rail tooltip as the body.
Move selection with onItemClick; exactly one selected item.
Group items under short section titles.
Use counters for actionable counts; notification dots for "something new".
Keep labels to one or two words; icons are required on the top level so the collapsed rail still works.
Remember the collapsed state per user.

With a custom brand (workspace logo + name), pass its logo as logoCollapsed too: the collapsed rail shows that mark centred over the items, at the same rail width as a Sidebar that starts collapsed. Without it the rail keeps the brand's first element, centred, and hides the rest visually.
Put account, settings and help in the footer, not between destinations.
Write each footer action as ; the collapsed rail hides the span visually, names the button from it and adds the 1s tooltip, so no extra aria-label or Tooltip is needed.
Show the Workspace variant only when users belong to more than one workspace; mark exactly one workspace item selected so its Focus-Ring shows which one is active.
Fill a SidebarSubMenu flyout with a `<Search variant="popover">` and Master items.
Wire onSubMenuClose so Escape and an outside press close the flyout, and give it a subMenuLabel.

Match background to the page Canvas (background layers): Canvas/Default → default, Canvas/Alt (white page) → alt, Canvas/Flat → flat so the navigation and page read as one surface in light and dark. Cards on that page use the same Surface.

Give a section title at most one action, as a Button/Icon-Flat Small (IconButton appearance="flat" level="primary" size="sm" with aria-label). Don't resize it — the sidebar centres it in a 16px wrapper so the title row keeps its height.
dont: Don't force hover/focus states in examples; use real interaction.
Don't nest more than one level.
Don't put primary actions ("New project") as nav items; use a Button in the page header.
Don't mix navigation and filters in the Sidebar.
Don't hide the only route to a destination inside a collapsed group.
Don't open a second flyout from a flyout.
Don't give one item both an inline tree (children) and a flyout.

date-picker.title: Date Picker
do: On a phone, let DateField open its sheet (it does at the mobile breakpoint), or open DatePickerSheet from your own row; for a range, update `summary` from onRangeChange so the price follows the picks.

On a phone, put an inline calendar in the screen or a Bottom Sheet: at the mobile breakpoint it takes the Figma mobile primitives by itself and fills the width; pass device="mobile" only to force them (a popover, a narrow preview).

Disable impossible dates (past check-in) with minDate / maxDate (earlier or later days disabled); in a DateField a typed date outside them is kept and marked aria-invalid, so pair the range with an `error` message.

Pass `today` (your app's date: a server, business or demo date) when it is not the device's; the Today ring and the month the calendar opens on follow it. DateField forwards `today`, `minDate` and `maxDate` to its calendar.
Show the chosen range and its consequence (nights, price) next to the calendar.
Let users type the date in the DateField; the calendar is a shortcut, not the only input.
Use calendar="dual" for ranges longer than a few days; single for one date.
Use the month-year picker for dates far from today (billing periods, expiries).
Close the popover after a single date is picked (no actions) and return focus to the field.

With showActions, commit in onApply(value, range): picks are a draft, Submit applies it and Cancel (or Escape) returns to the applied value. Inline, both stay disabled until there is a change, and Submit waits for a range's end date (harness: date-picker/actions-need-apply).
dont: Don't open the calendar for read-only DateFields.
Don't make users click back through years for birthdays; type the date or use the month-year picker.
Don't show Apply/Cancel for a single-date pick that can commit immediately.
Don't allow a range end before its start; the second click after an earlier date restarts the range.

Don't pass `month` without `onMonthChange`: Previous / Next and the month-year wheel stop working. To open on another month, keep it in state: `month={month} onMonthChange={setMonth}` (harness: interaction/controlled-needs-handler).

calendar.title: Calendar
do: Put CalendarToolbar above the view and move the period with shiftPeriod(date, view, ±1); Today returns to today's period.
Give every calendar a colour and keep it: Brand for the main calendar, the other hues only to tell calendars apart.
Pass `today` (and `now` for the Time-Grid) when your app's date is not the device clock, so Today and the now line agree with your data.
Open an event's details from onEventClick and set selectedEventId while they are open (State=Selected).
Give the Time-Grid a height (or max-height) so the hours scroll under the fixed day header.
dont: Don't put the page's main action (New event) in the Toolbar: it belongs to the page header; the Toolbar has only Tertiary buttons.
Don't use buttons for the view switch: the Toolbar's switch is a Segmented.
Don't put filters (which calendars) in the Toolbar: they are Chip advanced in the page's Control-Bar.
Don't colour events with Accent: Today and the now line are the only Accent on a grid.
Don't draw a week CalendarTimeGrid on a phone: it shows the 3-Day grid there.

schedule.title: Schedule
do: Keep the confirm action ("Book 10:00") in the page or sheet footer, enabled once a time is chosen.
Keep taken or past times in place (disabled, struck through) so the day keeps its rhythm.
Pass `now` (and `today`) when your app's clock is not the device's, so Past / Now and the now line agree with your data.
Give bars real start and end dates: a bar past the visible range scrolls with the track.
dont: Don't hide taken slots: people then cannot tell a full day from an empty one.
Don't use a Slot-Picker for filters or scopes: that is Chip advanced.
Don't put several Now stops in an itinerary: one stop runs at a time.
Don't stack many overlapping events in a Day-Planner: use CalendarTimeGrid, which splits the column.

timeline.title: Timeline
do: Use an Avatar marker when a person acted, an Icon when the system did, a Dot in compact logs.
Let the tone carry status: Positive approved, Negative rejected, Warning waiting, Accent the newest or current.
Name the Gantt after the plan (aria-label) so its table reads as more than "Tasks".
Keep bars on their real dates: the track scrolls; never squeeze a bar to fit.
dont: Don't colour markers for decoration: tone is status.
Don't use Milestones or the Gantt for a form the user steps through: use Stepper.
Don't mark more than one milestone Current.

tooltip.title: Tooltip
do: On a phone, where a tooltip never opens on touch, show a tip for a new action open from the start with its close X: <Tooltip closable open onOpenChange>.
Wrap a focusable trigger (Button, IconButton, link).
Keep text under ~80 characters, no punctuation for single phrases.
Use Accent briefly for confirmations ("Copied!").
Explain disabled controls in visible text; a disabled control can't be focused to reveal a tooltip.
Use a 1s hover delay (TOOLTIP_HOVER_DELAY, the default) and show at once on keyboard focus; moving to a neighbouring control within 600ms opens its tooltip without waiting.

Icon-only controls get their name tooltip for free (IconButton, Top/Bottom Navigation actions, close and remove buttons); add an explicit <Tooltip> only for a longer hint — the built-in one then stays silent.
dont: Don't put links or buttons inside a tooltip (its own close X, closable, is the one exception).
Don't repeat the visible label word for word.
Don't wrap a disabled control (harness: tooltip/disabled-trigger).
Don't rely on a hover tooltip on touch-first surfaces (use a closable one open from the start), and never for error messages.

tabs.title: Tabs
do: Use size medium (the default) on desktop and on phones; small only inside a genuinely narrow component space (a dense card header or table toolbar), never just to save room on a page; large only as the desktop top-navigation bar (64px, Indicator), never inside page content.
Give the tablist an aria-label and pair each tab with a TabPanel.
Keep 2–7 tabs with short labels.
Show counts with badges; hide at zero.
Keep the selected tab when the page reloads (URL or state).
Use fullWidth for 2–4 tabs that should split the width evenly (mobile headers); keep hugging tabs for longer sets.
dont: Don't use tabs to submit or navigate away.
Don't mix icon-only and labelled tabs.
Don't use more than 7 tabs or a single tab (harness: tabs/item-count).
Don't nest tab bars inside tab panels; use Segmented for the inner switch.

breadcrumbs.title: Breadcrumbs
do: On a phone (under 744) the trail gives way by itself in AppShellHeader and PageHeader: a Back to the parent crumb on a child page, nothing on a root (component-usage-rules §17). Keep passing the full trail; don't hide it yourself.
Make the last item the current page (not a link).
Collapse long paths with maxItems.
Use the same labels as page titles.
Start with the root (Home or the workspace) and use the master item's icon only there.
dont: Don't use breadcrumbs as the only navigation.
Don't highlight the master icon on its own on hover: the whole item takes Neutral/Flat/Hover and the icon stays Neutral/Strongest.
Don't include the current page as a link.
Don't show breadcrumbs on top-level pages (only one item).

progress.title: Progress
do: Label every progress (visible label or aria-label).
Use Status only when low values are a problem (quotas, health).
Switch to Status/green or Done when complete.
Keep the value a percentage from 0 to 100 (harness: progress/value-range).
Pair the percentage with the unit that matters ("12 / 48 MB", "3 of 5 steps").
Use layout="stacked" when the bar needs a name: label names it and valueLabel carries the unit ("Storage" · "68 GB of 100 GB"), on one row above the track.
Use scale="quota" for storage, seats or credits measured against a limit, so a nearly full quota turns Warning/Negative instead of green (harness: progress/quota-scale).
dont: Don't animate backwards.
Don't use colour alone to convey state.
Don't use a progress bar for unknown durations → Skeleton or a spinner.
Don't stop at 99% without explaining what's left.
