Don't build your own name + value row above an inline bar → layout="stacked" with label and valueLabel.

dialog.title: Modal & Dialog
do: Use Dialog for a notice or a quick confirm, with one field at most (type the name to delete). A data-entry form, two or more fields, opens in a ModalForm on desktop and tablet (harness: dialog/form-uses-modal-form) and in a BottomSheet on a phone (harness: modal-form/not-on-phone).
Use actionsDirection="vertical" on a Dialog when the choices deserve equal weight or labels are long; a ModalForm keeps its actions in a row (harness: modal-form/actions-horizontal).
Keep a ModalForm's side column (side) no taller than the form, a summary or an illustration, so the actions sit under the fields with no empty band; longer side content belongs in the form.
Phrase the title as the question ("Delete “Marketing site”?") and repeat the verb in the primary action.
Use theme negative + level danger for irreversible actions; give Cancel initial focus with `secondaryAction={{ label: "Cancel", autoFocus: true }}` (otherwise the primary action takes it).
Require typing the name for high-impact deletes.
Keep one primary action; a third (tertiary) action sits on the left.
Return focus to the element that opened the dialog.

Overlays portal through ZenPortal: when light/dark and the other modes are set on an inner element instead of <html>, wrap the app in <ZenPortalProvider container={el}> with an element inside that scope, so Modal, Dialog and Side Panel follow the mode. Inside a [data-zen-overlay-root] device frame the frame wins (as for Menu).
On a phone screen, put the unsaved-changes guard Dialog inside the PlatformPhone (any [data-zen-overlay-root] frame): it opens in the frame, with no ZenPortalProvider layer.

On a phone (viewport ≤ 480px or a phone frame) Dialog uses Device=Mobile (10153:7277): 350 of 390, with 20px side margins (Padding/Large), at the bottom of the screen above the home indicator, Heading/4 title and stacked full-width actions.

With onSubmit, ModalForm is a <form noValidate> like Form. Validate in onSubmit and set each field's `error`; `required` alone never blocks the submit. A blocked submit focuses the first invalid field and announces "N fields need attention" (invalidMessage overrides the text).
dont: Don't stack dialogs.
Don't use a dialog for information the user can ignore.
Don't hide the only way out (always Escape or a cancel action).
Don't open a dialog from a dialog (harness: dialog/no-nested).
Don't put a form in a Dialog, and don't open a ModalForm on a phone.
Don't open a dialog on page load without a user action.
Don't rely on the browser's required bubbles in a ModalForm. They are off by default; noValidate={false} only when you deliberately hand validation to the browser.

toast.title: Toast Message
do: Show toasts with `const { toast } = useToast(); toast({ title: "Invite sent" })`; ZenProvider hosts the stack, so no ToastStack state is needed.
Keep it to one short title and at most one line of description.
Offer a single action, and prefer Undo for actions that change data.

Let the action close its toast: Undo/View runs onClick and then dismisses it, so onClick needs no dismiss(id) (calling it anyway is harmless); set action.keepOpen only when the action updates the toast in place.
Use Neutral for everyday confirmations (sent, saved, copied); reserve colours for status that matters (Positive when success is the news, e.g. a payment went through).
Auto-dismiss informational toasts (about 5s, longer with an action) and pause on hover/focus.
Show one toast at a time for the same event; replace, don't stack duplicates.
Outside a ZenProvider (or for a second, custom host), render a ToastStack yourself: keep the list in state and remove items in onDismiss — it keeps timing, pause-on-hover and motion consistent.
dont: Don't use a toast to ask a question or confirm a destructive action.
Don't put essential information only in a toast. It disappears.
Don't show more than one action, or links inside the text.
Don't use Negative for errors the user must fix in a form; show them inline.
Don't ask a question or exceed ~60 characters in the title (harness: toast/concise).

alert-banner.title: Alert Banner
do: Place it at the top of the page or region it describes, above the content.
Match the theme to severity (Warning for upcoming problems, Negative for broken state).
Give Medium banners one clear action ("Update payment").
Let users dismiss non-critical banners and remember that choice.
dont: Don't stack several banners; merge them or show the most severe.
Don't give a Small banner an action (Figma Small has no Actions slot).
Don't use a banner for success after a single action; that's a Toast.

accordion.title: Accordion
do: Write titles users can scan, such as questions or clear topics.
Use one theme per list: Divider for long lists, Box for a few standalone items.
Open the item that matches the user's context (e.g. from a deep link).
Give rows with end-aligned values (a receipt, specs) contentWidth="full", so the values line up with the box edge; text keeps the default column.
dont: Don't hide critical or primary information inside a collapsed item.
Don't nest accordions inside accordions.
Don't put the only call to action inside a collapsed panel.
Don't nest (harness: accordion/no-nested).
Don't add a separate expand button or an onClick on the wrapper; the whole header row already toggles the section.

pagination.title: Pagination
do: Keep the current page visible and marked (aria-current).
Show first and last pages with an ellipsis for long ranges.
In tables, pick the page size with the Inline theme's Chip.
Scroll back to the top of the list after a page change.
dont: Don't paginate lists with only one or two pages.
Don't reset filters or sorting when the page changes.
Don't use numbered pages for unbounded feeds.
Don't paginate fewer than 3 pages (harness: pagination/worth-paging).

skeleton.title: Skeleton
do: Match the final layout: avatar → round shape, title → heading, paragraph → text lines.
Wrap the loading region in aria-busy=true with a visually hidden “Loading…” status.
Swap to real content in one step.
Respect reduced motion: the pulse turns off (harness: motion/reduced-motion).
dont: Don't show skeletons for content that loads instantly.
Don't use one big block for everything; it hides the structure.
Don't keep a skeleton on screen indefinitely; show an error or empty state.

divider.title: Divider
do: Use the Default color unless the design explicitly needs more emphasis.
Reserve High for the one line that closes a calculation (receipt totals).
Mark toolbar and label separators decorative when the groups are already labelled.
Let spacing do most of the grouping; add a divider only where groups would otherwise blur.
dont: Don't stack two dividers or put one at the very top/bottom of a card (harness: divider/no-double).
Don't use a divider as a container border.
Don't draw dashed dividers in Pale — dashed steps up to Subtle automatically.

shape.title: Shape
do: Colour shapes with tokens only: fill from Color/Background, stroke from Color/Border (no hex).
Give a shape that carries meaning a label (role=img); leave decoration unlabelled (hidden from assistive tech).
Use px insets only inside a free frame (a Box or Screen without auto layout); inside auto layout let the frame place it.
Keep a line's angle in rotation and its length in width, as Figma stores a LINE.
dont: Don't draw charts, progress or ratings from shapes: use the components that carry values and labels.
Don't use a Shape as a card or section background: use Box surface or Card.
Don't pass hex or rgb colours: fill and stroke take Zen token paths only.
Don't use an image fill for a picture in the content (an article photo, a product shot): use Image (alt, ratio, caption).
Don't write a vector's d with relative commands, arcs or H / V: Zen Studio and Figma read absolute M / L / C / Q / Z.

inline-message.title: Inline Message
do: Place it directly above or beside the content it's about.
Lead with the impact in the title, then the fix in the caption.
Offer at most one action, phrased as a verb ("View plans").
Keep the text Strongest (title) and Base (caption) of the theme; the icon carries the Light highlight.
Use Custom only with a real visual (harness: inline-message/custom-needs-visual).
dont: Don't render an empty message (harness: inline-message/needs-content).
Don't stack several inline messages; merge them or show the most severe.
Don't use Negative for a single invalid field; put the error on the field.
Don't make essential information dismissible.

empty-state.title: Empty State
do: Say what is empty in the title ("No projects yet", "No results for “tokns”").
Give the next step as a verb in primaryAction (Primary); a way out such as Clear filters or Clear search goes alone in secondaryAction (Tertiary) (harness: empty-state/way-out-tertiary).

Pick the size from where it sits: Medium (240) when the Empty State fills the page's main content — first run, a page with no results, no access; Small (200) when it fills one region of a page that still shows other content — a widget or Card, a table or list, a tab panel, a sidebar, side panel, sheet, popover or dialog (harness: empty-state/small-in-box; ChartCard sets Small for you).
Keep the illustration and swap its icon to match what is missing (icon="icon-folder-line").
Keep the caption to one sentence.
dont: Don't hide the illustration (illustration={false}): where space is short use size="sm" (harness: empty-state/keep-illustration).
Don't put a Medium Empty State in a widget, card or panel, or a Small one on a page that is empty.
Don't show an Empty State while data is still loading.
Don't leave a first-run screen without an action.
Don't use vague action labels (harness: empty-state/action-label).
Don't use more than two actions.

stepper.title: Stepper
do: Name the process with aria-label (harness: stepper/needs-label).
Keep 2–7 steps with short noun titles (harness: stepper/step-count).
Let users click back to passed steps to edit; keep future steps inert.
Mark a failed step with error and explain the fix next to it (Inline Message).
dont: Don't let users skip ahead to unvisited steps unless every step is optional.
Don't use a stepper for navigation between unrelated pages.
Don't hide the current step's title on small screens; switch to vertical instead.

slider.title: Slider
do: Use a Solid icon for the leading Icon (it sits inside the filled track): icon-volume-max-solid, icon-sun-solid.
Always name it (harness: slider/needs-name) and give valueText for units ("40%", "120 gigabytes").
Show the current value next to the slider when the number matters.
Use step for quantities with natural increments.
Preview the effect live while dragging (volume, size).
dont: Don't use White at Small — it doesn't exist (harness: slider/white-no-small).
Don't use a slider for precise values without a way to type them.
Don't put two sliders controlling the same value on one screen.

slider-field.title: Slider Field
do: Label the number with what it changes ("Offset X", "Overlay Opacity") and show its unit through formatValue.
Pick min, max and step so the fill means something: the whole field is the range.
Stack rows of one group Spacing/Gap/XSmall apart, as inline fields.
dont: Don't use it where the number does not matter; a Slider is calmer (harness: slider-field/value-in-range keeps the start value inside the range).
Don't make the range so wide that one pixel jumps many steps; people then type instead of scrubbing.

curve-preview.title: Curve Preview
do: Put it right above the settings it previews and pass the same values (type, bounce), so the curve follows every change.
Let it take the panel's width: the height stays 176 and the curve stretches with the width.
Name it after the setting when the type alone is not enough ("Back photo transition: Spring, bounce 0.3").
dont: Don't use it as a chart of data; it has no axes or values to read.
Don't pass a bounce outside 0–1 or a bounce to an ease curve (harness: curve-preview/bounce-range).

card.title: Card
do: On a phone, count the cards in the group: three or more side by side (a row of stats, a grid of projects, a list of choices) take spacing="small"; one or two cards, such as a single box around a list, keep Spacing=Medium, the default (harness card/spacing-by-count). A card around a Voice frame stays Small: the frame pads itself (Spacing/Padding/XLarge). Desktop cards keep Medium whatever their number.

Use one theme per grid. With nothing else deciding (examples, a page with no Sidebar), theme="default" on Canvas/Default: no border, no shadow (usage rules §16). On a Canvas/Flat page, Flat-Border: Surface/Flat inside a Pale frame. Shadow when the screen's Sidebar casts one, Border on a white page, inside another surface or on a clickable card, On-Container inside a Dialog, ModalForm, SidePanel or BottomSheet (on their Container fill; harness card/on-container-in-overlay), Pale/Semi-Pale on imagery.

Match the screen's elevation to its Sidebar: the default Sidebar (Surface + shadow) on the grey Canvas takes Shadow cards with no border; a white Canvas takes a Surface-alt or Flat Sidebar (optionally with divider) and Border cards. Never a shadowed Sidebar on a white Canvas.
Title a widget card with Heading/Subheading (heading level from the outline); page sections outside cards use Heading/4.
Make the whole card clickable when it opens one thing, and name it with aria-label when the content doesn't start with a title.
Use Active for the selected card in a single-choice grid, together with aria-pressed or a radio inside.
Put secondary card actions in the Sub-Action menu.
Card shadow = Box effectStyle="Shadow/Bottom/Level-1": a static elevated panel may be a Box with that style; a clickable or selectable panel is a Card.

Pick surface from the page Canvas: default on Canvas/Default, surface="alt" passed explicitly on a white Canvas/Alt page, theme="flat-border" on a Canvas/Flat page. Only an explicit alt drops the Shadow theme's shadow; a page-scope --zen-card-surface suits Border or Default cards only, which is what a Canvas/Alt page takes anyway.

Put colour on a box by the page's Canvas: theme="subtle" and a color on the grey Canvas/Default (Pale fades into it), theme="pale" on a white Canvas/Alt or Canvas/Flat page (any of the nine hues, content stays neutral), e.g. a card per project or client (harness card/pale-on-canvas-default).
Let at most one widget per row stand out with theme="solid"; the dark widget is Solid Neutral, a hue (brand, cyan, yellow, orange) or accent suits one time-sensitive figure.

Write a Solid card's content as on any card: Text, Heading, Icon, charts, ProgressBar and the ⋮ read the fill's own family by themselves (content follows the fill, user 2026-10-17): Content/Inverse/* on Neutral, Content/On-Colors on Brand, Cyan and Orange, Content/On-Brights on Yellow, Content/On-Accent on Accent. MetricTrend and a MetricCard tile's Dock-Icon follow too (Inverse on Neutral, On-Color on the others). Pick Button appearance="overlay" level="inverse" on Solid Neutral, a Primary button on a Solid hue (Figma Metric-Card Hero).
On Brand, Cyan, Orange and Accent the white On-Colors text measures about 3:1: keep what you write there short and large (the number, a title), and put long or small text on another card.

Pricing plans: Default cards in an auto-fit grid; Active marks the current plan, an Accent Badge marks the recommended one, and each card ends with one md CTA pinned to the bottom whose label says what happens (Upgrade to Pro · Switch · Manage plan).
dont: Don't put buttons, links or inputs inside a clickable card (harness: card/clickable-no-nested-controls).
Don't nest cards inside cards.
On a phone, don't leave three or more cards at Medium, or shrink a card on its own to Small.
Don't frame a static card with Subtle — Border uses Pale until the card is clickable (§6).
Don't put a Pale card on the grey Canvas/Default: it fades into the page; use theme="subtle" (harness card/pale-on-canvas-default).
Don't use Active as decoration; it means selected.
Don't make a whole row Solid: one widget stands out, the rest share the row's theme.
Don't set data-theme or a dark mode on one card to darken it: one page is one mode, and theme="solid" color="neutral" re-points only its content tokens.
Don't put fields, Search or other Surface controls on a Solid card; they keep the page's Surface fill.

dock-icon.title: Dock Icon
do: Use Subtle in dense lists and tables; Solid for app tiles and hero marks.
Keep one size per list (Small in tables, Medium in lists).
Leave it decorative (no label) when the name is next to it.
Map colours consistently to categories across the product.
dont: Don't make a Dock Icon a button on its own; wrap it in a labelled control.
Don't use Theme=Emoji without an emoji (harness: dock-icon/emoji-needs-glyph).
Don't use it for people — that's an Avatar.

voice.title: Voice
do: Put them on a Card or a Surface: the frame itself is transparent (Figma).
Wire every action you show: a main action without its handler does nothing (harness: voice/actions-wired).

Let your audio code drive state, and give the time and levels from it: one recorder level every 1/7 s (oldest dropped) keeps a real take scrolling at the timeline's speed; leave levels unset in a prototype and the sample moves by itself.
On a phone, use a white screen (canvas surface) so the Surface/Alt signal and card show.
dont: Don't start recording or listening without a press: the microphone stays off until Record / Start talking.
Don't hide the state's meaning in colour alone: the Badge and the guidance line say it in words.
Don't use AiVoiceConversation for a recording to send: that is VoiceRecorder.

list-item.title: List Item
do: Give a ListBox footer action ("Open calendar", "Go to Inbox") as a Tertiary Button (the Button default), straight in the footer: it fills the box on desktop and tablet and hugs its label on mobile (harness: listbox/footer-action-tertiary).
Make a settings row that is one on/off switch a <ToggleListItem>, not a ListItem with a Toggle in its trailing slot.
Wrap rows in <List aria-label> so the group is named.

Put a box of List-Item rows in <ListBox> (header and footer optional) instead of a Box or Card you pad yourself: its Card-padding-medium and 2XLarge corners are right on every device. Content that is not rows (a DescriptionList, labelled Toggles, a form) goes in a Card.

Pick the ListBox theme by where it sits (usage rules §16): default on Canvas/Default and on a Surface-Alt phone screen; flat-border on a Canvas/Flat page; shadow beside a default Sidebar (elevation follows the Sidebar); border on a white page (Canvas/Alt, a white phone screen) or inside another Surface (a Card); on-container inside a Dialog, ModalForm, SidePanel or BottomSheet (their Container fill; harness listbox/on-container-in-overlay).
Make the whole row the target (onClick / href) when it opens one thing; for drill-down add a passive chevron.

Put quick actions in the trailing slot as Button/Icon-Flat Medium (IconButton appearance="flat" size="md") with an aria-label. They work on clickable rows too — Figma keeps the trailing action in Hover, Pressed and Selected — and stay separate targets that don't open the row.
Keep to one or two trailing actions; move the rest into a More (…) menu.

Make a See all / Show all at a section head (beside a ListBox header title or a kicker) underlined text, not a button (user, 2026-10-13: it takes no more room than its words): <Text as="span" textStyle="Body/Base/Medium"><Link tone="inherit"> — href when it opens the full list, as="button" with aria-expanded when it expands the list in place.

Give a row that ends in an amount or total value + valueCaption (a transaction: "+94,860,000 VND" over "3,600.00 USD") instead of a Text stack in trailing: it lines up with the title and caption and keeps its width. Keep the sign in the text (+ / −) when valueTone colours money in or out.

Use titleLines={2} when the title must be read in full (long task, document or file names in a narrow list); keep the default one line in dense lists where the caption carries the detail. Keep the caption short (it may wrap to a second line).
Mark the current row with selected (Active/Neutral/Subtle), not a custom fill.

Pick the Figma case by what the row does: Interactive (onClick or href) when the whole row opens, selects or navigates; static (neither) when it only shows information, even with trailing buttons. Both pad Padding/Small (12px) above and below and nothing at the sides; Interactive only adds the fill and its states.

Give every list its side inset from the container: a ListBox (Card-padding-medium), or the page margin on a full-bleed phone screen (Box paddingX="lg" paddingY="xs"). Leave at least 12px beside clickable rows so the fill is not clipped.

On a phone, make the list that closes the page (transactions, tasks, activity: nothing after it, not in a widget grid) an open section, as Figma's ◆ Finance Transactions: a title row (Heading/4 and its See all Link) over a <List> at the page margin, straight on the screen, no ListBox (usage rules §19, user rule 2026-10-21; harness: listbox/closing-list-on-phone). Lists in a widget grid, inside a box, and grouped settings lists (§15) keep their ListBox.

Split long settings into groups: a visible group header per group and one List per group named after it (aria-label or aria-labelledby). The header is a Heading one level below the nearest heading above (h2 on a screen whose h1 is the title), Body/Small/Bold in tone "light" (Content/Neutral/Light, 3.7:1 — Apple's 3:1 for bold text): a kicker label, not a Strongest title.

Keep the row title in its Body/Base/Bold (Figma Info-Content Title) on read and unread rows alike. Mark unread with a dot or Badge plus a visually hidden "Unread" (WCAG 1.3.1); the caption may go Strongest.
A kicker above a ListBox lines up with the row text: Box paddingX="xl" (24px) on desktop, paddingX="lg" (20px) on a phone, xs (8px) above the box.
dont: Don't write a footer action as plain text or a Link: it reads as a caption and has no button target. Don't wrap its Button in a <Stack align="start">: it would hug on desktop and tablet too.
Don't make only the chevron or a trailing button the way to open the row — the whole row is the target.
Don't put a Toggle or Checkbox on a clickable row: the row click and the switch compete. Make the row flip the switch, or keep the row static (harness: list-item/clickable-row-toggle).
Don't use Small or text buttons in the trailing slot; trailing actions are Medium icon buttons (harness: list-item/trailing-button-medium).
Don't mix leading sizes in one list — row heights stop lining up.
Don't put a Main (bordered) Button for See all / Show all in a section head; it is underlined text (a Link).
Don't pad the rows — no padding on .zen-list-item, no <List inset> (deprecated); inset the List with its container (harness: list-item/inset-not-padding).
Don't put a list of clickable rows flush against an edge or a clipping scroller: its fill hangs 12px outside the content; leave Padding/Small (12px) or more around it.
Don't give a static row an onClick just to get hover, and don't mark a static row selected.
Don't use a list for data users compare across columns.
Don't hand-build rows (a div with a Text and a Badge or Button); use ListItem so padding, hit area and focus are consistent.
Don't make a row title a heading, and don't signal unread by weight alone.
Don't make group labels inside a Menu, Popover, Select or Listbox headings; they are labels.
Don't box the list that closes a phone page in a ListBox (a Transactions or To-do list under the screen's widgets): it joins the page as an open section (§19).

Don't put content that is not List-Item rows (a DescriptionList, Toggles, a form) in a ListBox — use a Card. Don't frame a ListBox on Canvas/Default with border or shadow when no condition asks for it, and never give a ListBox on Surface-Alt or a Pale fill a drop shadow (§9).

Don't give a ListBox a color unless it is theme="pale", or surface="alt" unless it is default or border: Figma's List-Box has no such variant and the code ignores it (harness: listbox/color-ignored, listbox/surface-ignored).

table.title: Table
do: Name the table (aria-labelledby pointing at its section heading, a caption, or aria-label; harness: table/needs-name).

Title a table that is its own page section with a Heading/4 h2 right above it; a table inside a widget Card takes the widget title, Heading/Subheading, like every widget title (harness: table/title-heading-4).
Right-align numbers and amounts; keep text left.
Give each row one primary text (bold) and at most one caption.

Put row actions in the last column as Button/Icon-Flat Medium: `content: "actions"` with the column's `actions` (no cell function), or TableActions with IconButton appearance="flat" level="primary" in a `cell`; a ⋯ Menu trigger for several (harness: table/actions-flat).

Give a selectable table its bulk actions through bulkActions: at most 5 actions (icon + label + onClick, grouped by `group`) whose labels say how many rows they touch ("Archive 3 projects"); the Table draws the buttons, adds Clear selection and the count, and moves what doesn't fit into a More menu.
Show an Empty State row when filters return nothing.
Make only the fields people routinely correct editable; keep IDs, computed and audit columns read-only.
Wire onCommit to save, and validate numbers and required text; the error stays in the cell until fixed (harness: table/editor-needs-commit, table/editor-number-validate).
Right-align number editors like the numbers they edit (harness: table/editor-number-right).
Use select for closed sets and tags for open sets; lock rows that can't change with edit.disabled.
Offer onOpen when the full record of an editable row needs a detail view; a read-only table that opens records uses onRowClick, so the whole row is the click target.
Let clickable content inside an editable cell (Tag onClick, links, buttons) keep its own action — clicking the cell around it edits. Leave room (padding, gaps) so the edit target stays easy to hit.

A table that is the page content or a section of it sits straight on the page: no Card, Box or other container and no Surface fill, and it spans the page width with no max: wrap that page in <Container maxWidth="full"> (not the default lg 1280). Only a table that is a widget (a dashboard tile with its own title and a few rows beside other widgets) goes in a Card.

Inside a surface (Card, ChartCard, an Accordion panel, SidePanel, Dialog/ModalForm, BottomSheet, Popover, a Box with a surface or border) the last row has no bottom rule: the surface edge closes the table. The Table drops it by itself; in Figma set the last row's cells to a 0 bottom stroke weight (the colour stays bound). A page table on the canvas keeps its last rule.

A table that is its own section gets an h2 in Heading/4 directly above it (<Heading level={2} id>), and the Table points to it with aria-labelledby. Use `caption` (rendered in Heading/4) only to name a table that already sits under a section heading: a caption is not a heading and is missing from the headings list (harness: table/title-heading-4).

Build cells from the cell primitives at their Figma sizes: Badge Medium (not Small) in Badge/Trend cells, media sized by Subtext (Avatar XSmall → Small and Icon base → lg and Dock Icon XSmall → Small when a caption is on) (harness: table/media-size-by-subtext), Avatar/Stack Small for groups.
dont: Don't make selectable or sortable tables without handlers (harness: table/interaction-needs-handler).
Don't open a read-only row from a small icon or the hover Open button: use onRowClick (a passive chevron at the end may show that rows open).
Don't count on long text wrapping: rows stay one line and cut it with an ellipsis, so show the full value on the detail view (onRowClick or onOpen).
Don't use colour alone for status — use a Badge with text.
Don't make every cell editable — it turns the table into a spreadsheet and invites accidental edits.
Don't commit on every keystroke; the editor saves on Enter, Tab, Escape (valid values) or clicking another cell.
Don't hide the saved result: show the new value immediately and confirm or undo in a Toast when the change is significant.
Don't title a table with a Body/…/Bold label (it reads as a row label) or with a Text styled Heading/4 (a paragraph, not a heading); use a Heading level 2 in Heading/4.

rating.title: Rating
do: Ask one clear question as the aria-label and visible heading (harness: rating/needs-name).
Show the meaning of the current star value in words ("Great").
Use RatingDisplay with the review count next to it; never show an average without its sample size.
Follow a low score with an optional "what went wrong?" field.
OpinionScale: keep custom labels to one or two short words. Longer text is clamped to two lines with an ellipsis, and the full text still names the radio.

NpsScale: keep scale={10} for NPS: the detractor/passive/promoter split needs all 11 points. Under 264px of width it wraps into two rows (0–5 over 6–10) with the low label above 0 and the high label under 10, so don't switch to scale={5} to save space.
dont: Don't use the star input to display an average — use RatingDisplay.
Don't make a rating required before users can continue unless it's the task.
Don't mix scales on one screen (stars and NPS for the same question).

color-selector.title: Color Selector
do: Name the group (harness: rating/needs-name) and give every swatch a colour name.
Use token colours so swatches follow light/dark mode.
Keep 5–12 swatches; order them by hue.
Preview the effect of the colour next to the selector.
dont: Don't rely on colour alone to convey meaning; the name is announced and shown on hover.
Don't use a light swatch without contrast="dark" — the white check disappears.
Don't pass raw hex/rgb swatch values; use var(--zen-color-background-support-<hue>-solid) and map the value back to your id (harness: color-selector/token-values).

color-picker.title: Color Picker
do: Give ColorField a label that names what the colour is for ("Brand colour"), not "Colour".
Keep the picker's saved colours to the palette people reuse (the brand, the last picks), 6 at most so they fit one row.
Pass hex values ("#1F6FEB") to value and savedColors; store the hex the field returns.
dont: Don't use ColorField to pick a status or a Zen token: those come from the system (harness: color-picker/hex-value).
Don't pass a CSS colour name, rgb() or a token as ColorField or ColorPicker value: the field shows and returns a hex (harness: color-picker/hex-value).
Don't place a ColorSwatch as the only cue of meaning; name it or show the value beside it.

metric.title: Metric Widget
do: Format the value with units and separators (harness: metric/formatted-value).
Give a typed MetricCard the data its type draws: series, goal, comparison or categories (harness: metric/type-data).
Pass categories largest first and keep them to 2–7 (harness: metric/category-count).
Pass format so the series summary, the goal's label and the category amounts read like the number ("$105.7K", "1,284 h").
Always say what the trend compares against ("vs. last month").
Use the same size for metrics in one row; one hero metric at most.
Pair a worrying trend with guidance (Inline Message) or a link to details.
Colour-code metrics by category with the Dock-Icon theme (Revenue green, Users blue…) and keep that mapping across the product.
Use a Solid Dock-Icon only for the one metric that should lead (a goal, or an error that needs action).
dont: Don't colour the number itself to show good/bad — the trend badge carries it.
Don't show more than ~4 KPI cards in a row; group or prioritise.
Don't round away meaningful precision in finance values.
Don't give every tile a different colour for decoration, or rely on the icon colour alone for good/bad; the trend badge carries the status.

uploader.title: Uploader
do: State allowed types and the size limit before upload (harness: uploader/accept-caption).
Label the field (harness: uploader/needs-label).
Show progress and time left; let users cancel an upload.
Explain rejected files on the item and offer Retry.
Use Replaceable for single-file fields such as an avatar.
For a single file, let the File-Item take the field's place: omit onReplace to re-open the picker, or pass one that really replaces the file.
Use extended={false} (48px row) where vertical space is tight, e.g. inside a table row or a dense form.
dont: Don't reject files silently.
Don't hide the browse option — the drop zone is also a button.
Don't upload before the user confirms when files are sensitive.
Don't pass a no-op onReplace (() => {}) — the Replace action would do nothing; omit it so Replace re-opens the picker (harness: uploader/no-noop-replace).

side-panel.title: Side Panel
do: Open it from the thing it describes and return focus there on close.
Use Modal when the page behind must pause; Standard when users keep working alongside it.
Keep one primary action; put Cancel as the secondary.
Keep contents to one column of fields or a list.

Overlays portal through ZenPortal: when light/dark and the other modes are set on an inner element instead of <html>, wrap the app in <ZenPortalProvider container={el}> with an element inside that scope, so Modal, Dialog and Side Panel follow the mode.
dont: Don't use a side panel for destructive confirmations (harness: side-panel/not-for-confirmations).
Don't stack side panels or open a Dialog from one unless it confirms a destructive step.
Don't hide the close control.

file-icon.title: File Icon
do: Put it next to the file name in uploads, attachments and lists.
Pick the format with fileIconFormatOf(file.name) instead of hard-coding.
Keep one size per list (36 in uploader items, 24–32 in dense lists).
dont: Don't use it as an action icon or inside a Button (harness: file-icon/not-an-action).
Don't show a generic doc when a specific format exists.
Don't recolour it; the base colour encodes the type.

flag.title: Flag
do: Put the country name or code next to the flag (Figma: flags alone are inaccessible).
Use the Figma Name exactly (harness: flag/unknown-name).
Match the size of the other leading visuals in the list (Avatar Cell 24 in tables, 32 in list rows).
Keep the round shape; never stretch or crop it.
dont: Don't use emoji flags — they differ per OS and Windows shows letters (harness: flag/no-emoji-flag).
Don't use a flag as the only label of a button or option.
Don't recolour or outline flags.

icon.title: Icon
do: Use line icons by default and solid for selected/filled states and remove affordances (icon-x-circle-solid).
Mark icons decorative when a text label is present.
Pair a meaningful standalone icon with aria-label or title.
Match icon size to the text beside it (base 20px next to Body/Base).
dont: Don't use an icon alone as the only label of an action without aria-label.
Don't mix line and solid icons in one toolbar.
Don't recolour icons with raw values; use Content tokens (harness: color/token-only in component CSS).
Don't scale icons with CSS transforms; use the size prop.
Don't pass size names from other components ("small", "medium"); any other string reaches CSS and the SVG falls back to its intrinsic size (harness: icon/size-token).

top-navigation.title: Top Navigation
do: An Avatar in the bar or beside the large title (the account, a profile photo) is drawn at the action size, Navigation-Action/Size 44, whatever Avatar size you pass (user 2026-10-19).

Give the bar the colour of the screen under it (user rule 2026-10-08): on Canvas/Default or Surface/Alt (the same colour in light and dark; a phone screen by default) use alt, compact-alt or alt-blurring; on a white Surface screen default, compact or default-blurring; an overlay type only on media.
Match the type to the page Canvas: Default on Surface, Alt on an Alt canvas, Compact on dense detail screens, an overlay type only on media.
Use a large title only on top-level screens (tab roots); a pushed screen with Back uses the bar title alone.

On a root, keep the default: the bar row folds into the large-title row (Figma Top-bar=false), so the actions sit at the right of the large title and stay put when it folds; pass topBar only for a stack that keeps the bar above the large title.

Put the line above a large title (a greeting, a brand) in largeTitleCapline and the line under it (a count, a room) in largeTitleSubheading, not in the title text: the title stays the heading's name and both fold away with it.

Pass a Badge or an Avatar straight in trailing (or largeTitleAction) as Figma's Trailing-Slot holds them, not inside an icon action; an account Avatar is size md or lg (Figma Medium 48 / Large 56 at Comfortable density). A visual is not a button: a tappable one needs its own labelled button.
Use topBar={false} without a large title only for a screen that starts with a brand band or a hero (Figma D2): keep title for screen readers, or leave it out when the content draws the h1.
Pin a status that must stay in view (offline, syncing, read-only) with banner, a Small AlertBanner: it sits under the bar and the control bar, edge to edge, and never scrolls away.
Let the large title follow the scroll with scrollRef instead of switching collapsed on a scrollTop threshold: it moves with the finger, never makes the content jump, and settles open or closed.

Let the title be the screen's h1 and start the content headings at h2: the large title (Heading/1) on a root screen, the compact bar title (Body/Extra/Bold) on a child screen and once the large title collapses. Don't add a second, hidden h1.
Set document.title to the screen title, then the app name, on every screen (WCAG 2.4.2).
Give every icon-only action a label; put a dot on the action (not the title) for unread states.
Keep at most three trailing actions, and three beside the large title, as Figma's Trailing-Slot takes (harness: top-navigation/max-three-trailing).
Draw Back with a left chevron (icon-chevron-left-line-medium, label "Back") on mobile and tablet (harness: navigation/back-chevron).
Keep the Figma rhythm: leading actions 16 apart, two flat trailing actions 20 apart; an H2 expand heading has 14px vertical padding.
Put a Segmented in the control bar with fullWidth; its items split the bar equally.

For a conversation header use the identity: Default type, compact margin, Tertiary back chevron, Avatar Large (or ChatAvatarGroup size="large") as titleLeading, presence as subtitle ("Active now" / "Active 2h ago") and the calls as one grouped pill (trailingGroup).

When the control bar is a Search and the bar collapses on scroll, pass searchAction: the Search folds into a top-right Search action and comes back as a bar on scroll up. Its onClick scrolls back up and focuses the field (harness: top-navigation/search-folds-to-action).
dont: Don't mix action styles in one bar (a Tertiary back with Flat trailing actions).
Don't use an overlay type over plain surfaces; its white content needs imagery behind it.
Don't put primary form actions (Save) in the bar and again at the bottom of the screen.
Don't put a status banner in controlBar or let it scroll away with the content: it reports the whole screen, so it belongs in banner.
Don't use a left arrow (icon-arrow-left-*) for Back: on mobile and tablet the chevron is the platform back affordance, arrows mean moving content.
Don't keep three other trailing actions next to a searchAction; while collapsed the Search takes a slot (harness: top-navigation/max-three-trailing).
Don't remove the large title from the layout on scroll (collapsed from an onScroll threshold): the content jumps by the title's height and can flip the state back.

bottom-navigation.title: Bottom Navigation
do: Keep 3–5 destinations (harness: bottom-navigation/destinations).
Use a solid glyph for the selected state (selectedIcon) and keep the label as the accessible name.
Use Floating Glass over imagery: idle icons are Neutral/Strongest and the selection defaults to Subtle; switch to Solid only for extra emphasis.
Clear the dot as soon as the destination is opened.
Over photos or video, pass backdrop="none" so the pill floats on the image; the Surface fade is for plain screens.
dont: Don't navigate to a destination that is not a root screen, or open a modal from a destination.
Don't hide the bar while the keyboard is closed or change the order between screens.
Don't use the action slot for anything but the app's primary create action.
Don't leave the Surface fade under a floating bar on a media screen; it shows as a white strip across the image.

bottom-sheet.title: Bottom Sheet
do: Keep one task per sheet and one primary action.
On a phone, open a form in a BottomSheet (its title, the fields, the actions in its footer), never in a ModalForm (harness: modal-form/not-on-phone).
Let the user drag, tap the scrim or press Escape to dismiss.

For a single choice, fill the sheet with List + ListItem: the picked row is `selected` (Active/Neutral/Subtle) with a trailing check, and picking closes the sheet. The Action type's `selectedId` row (Accent/Subtle) is Figma's state, not the house pattern for choices (user, 2026-09-30).
Lists inside the sheet use List/ListItem (the sheet sets --zen-list-inset: 0).
For long reading content (terms, release notes) use size="max" with vertical actions: the body scrolls under the fixed header and the footer stays reachable.
A sheet with fields is a form: pass onSubmit so Enter submits and the primary action is the submit button; close the sheet from the handler once the save succeeds.
Let a form sheet (onSubmit) start on its first field. Add data-autofocus only to start on a different control, never on the first field (redundant).
dont: Don't give an Action sheet no items (harness: bottom-sheet/action-needs-items).
Don't stack a sheet on a sheet; replace the content instead.
Don't put destructive actions first; mark them `destructive` and keep them last.
Don't nest a <Form> inside a BottomSheet that has onSubmit, and don't submit from primaryAction.onClick; pass form.handleSubmit to onSubmit instead.

chat.title: Chat
do: Show the avatar once per run of messages (on the last one) and the name only in groups.

Pass `author` for every message from others (harness: chat/others-need-author); for people without a photo pass `author={{ name }}`: message avatars show first + last name initials ('Nguyen Van Bao' → 'NB'), like the conversation list.

Match the device: in a phone use the Mobile pieces (ChatThread/ChatComposer device="mobile", hold to react, TopNavigation header); in a desktop window use device="desktop" (516px text, 400px photos, 40px Chat-Control, a Button/Icon-Flat thread header) where the hold layer is off and the Hover toolbar + right-click / Shift+F10 More menu take over (audit: device).
Put status ("Seen") under your last message only.
Use ChatFile for attachments so the file type colour and size are consistent.
Put Business conversations on Canvas/Default so the near-white Others bubble reads; Social threads sit on Surface.

Let ChatThread keep itself pinned to the latest message: it opens at the bottom and follows new messages, also after web fonts and photos settle, until the reader scrolls up. Don't add scroll-to-bottom effects or timers around it.
Keep a message that failed to send in the thread with failed + onRetry (Not delivered · Retry); Retry shows Sending… then the normal status.
Use call states in the conversation list (missed calls in Negative, ongoing in Positive) and a Bold title only for unread conversations.
On mobile, give every message hold-to-react: holdActions (chatHoldActions.others / .you / .call) and onReact; mark Delete destructive (harness: chat/hold-delete-destructive).

On desktop (ChatThread device="desktop") pass holdActions and onReact: each message gets the Figma Hover toolbar beside the bubble — Text/File React · Reply · More, Photo Share · React · More, Call More (Button/Icon-Flat Small Secondary, 8px from the bubble, mirrored for your messages). It uses the same chatHoldActions as the mobile hold menu; More lists the ones not shown. On desktop the whole message row is the hover target, not just the bubble.
Call bubbles take no reactions: holding (mobile) or hovering (desktop) a call shows only its actions (chatHoldActions.call — Report · Delete).
Use ChatAvatarGroup for group conversations: Medium (40px, 28px avatars) in lists, Small (32px, 20px avatars) in compact rows.
Use one action list for both inputs: the same holdActions drive the mobile hold menu and the desktop hover toolbar (its More menu).
Pick hold/hover actions with chatHoldActionsFor(kind, side): text & photos by side, files get Reply · Forward · Pin · Delete (Figma Focused/File), calls Call back · (Report) · Delete.

Reply: the Reply action sets the composer's replyTo (“Replying to …” bar, × / Escape cancel via onCancelReply — harness: chat/reply-cancellable); attach it to the sent message as replyTo and give every message an id so the quote can jump back. The quote previews the original by kind — text (2 lines), photo(s) with a thumbnail, file, call, voice, or “Message unavailable”. The composer moves focus into its field when a reply is set or switched (not on mount), so apps add no focus code of their own.
Keep the Reaction-Bar "+": let it open the built-in emoji panel, or pass onMore only when you ship a fuller picker; never wire it to a placeholder.

Keep every interaction live wherever Chat is shown: each message can be held (mobile) / hovered (desktop) for its Figma action set and reactions, Reply fills the composer and the sent quote jumps back, cards open, calls call back, the composer's actions and send work — never a no-op handler (harness: chat/no-locked-interaction; platform examples use useChatDemo).

Make deleting a message undoable: remove it at once and show a Toast with Undo (title 'Message deleted'); don't ask first. Move focus to the next message, and on Undo back to the restored one. Platform examples get this from useChatDemo().
ChatFile and ChatCall keep Figma's 32px text box in the 20/16 (Dashboard) scale and hug their lines in the mobile (and Popular) type scale. Don't override their heights.
Pass `by` for every reaction so pressing the pill shows who reacted; the "You" row removes your own reaction (harness: chat/reactions-name-people).
dont: Don't colour your own bubble with anything but Bubble-Chat-You.
Don't show timestamps on every bubble in Social; group by time with a ChatDateDivider.
Don't hand-build conversation rows; use ChatConversationItem (a ListItem).

Don't pin the thread to the bottom with justify-content:flex-end — overflowing messages become unreachable; ChatThread uses margin-top:auto on its first child (harness: layout/scroll-anchor-flex-end).
Don't silently drop a message that failed to send.
Don't hide message actions behind a hover-only toolbar on mobile; a long press opens the reactions and menu, like the platform does.

Don't give the call card a Secondary button: Figma Chat/Bubble/Call uses Button/Overlay Inverse (Social: Call back · Call again) and Button/Flat Primary on missed calls only (Business: Call back · Send voice message).

ai-chat.title: AI Chat
do: Show Stop while an answer streams and hide feedback actions until it finishes.
Offer 3–4 suggestions in the empty state that start real tasks.
Name every action (Copy, Regenerate, Good response); make thumbs toggle buttons (pressed).
Use the Surface field on a Surface-less canvas and Liquid Glass only over imagery.
When an answer fails, keep the question and show a Negative Inline Message in the thread with Try again; the retry streams like a normal answer.
Show the thinking dots (thinking, or streaming with no text yet) from the moment the prompt is sent until the first words arrive; never a static "Thinking…" text.
dont: Don't show actions on a streaming answer (harness: ai-chat/no-actions-while-streaming).
Don't put the user's prompt in an AI-styled bubble or the answer in a You bubble.
Don't hide the model switch behind an icon without a label.
Don't use Buttons for prompt suggestions; they are Chip/Normal Medium Secondary with an icon, like Figma.

chart.title: Chart
do: Size a Donut or Radial by name, as Figma's Size: small 120 (a tile, several charts in a row; the centre shows the figure alone), medium 168 (a chart card, the default), large 240 (a wide card, the total beside the ring), xlarge 320 (a hero card) (harness: chart/ring-size-named). A stretched Chart Card grows the ring from there.
Always give the chart an aria-label that says what it shows and over which range (harness: chart/needs-name).
Format values for people (`$23.4K`, `52 GB`, `1,990 h`) with `format`.

Keep the legend whenever colour tells series, slices or rings apart (harness: chart/stack-needs-legend, chart/shares-need-legend, chart/series-need-legend) and the heatmap's Less → More scale (harness: chart/heatmap-needs-scale).
Mark a forecast `projected` so it reads as not earned yet; show a goal as a `target` track, not as another series.
Use the Segmented range switch in the card instead of separate charts per range, and key the chart by the range so it draws in again.
Turn on showAverage when the question is "above or below normal?"; leave it off when the trend itself is the point.

Rank a BarList yourself, largest first, and fold the tail into "Other" past 8 rows (harness: chart/bar-list-ranked, chart/bar-list-rows); keep a BulletChart to 1–4 goals (harness: chart/bullet-rows); pass a GaugeChart its `max` when the value isn't a percentage (harness: chart/gauge-in-range); give a FunnelChart 3–6 stages in order, each no larger than the one before (harness: chart/funnel-stages).

Give an AreaChart one series, or 2–4 with type="stacked" (harness: chart/area-series-count); keep a GroupedBarChart to 2–3 series (harness: chart/grouped-series-count); name both measures of a ComboChart with barLabel and lineLabel (harness: chart/combo-needs-labels).
Lead the card with the figure the chart explains (`value`) and say what it is (`description`).
dont: Don't use a line for categories that aren't ordered in time.
Don't pick custom colours outside the chart palette unless a series has a fixed brand colour.
Don't put a chart where the user needs exact values; add a Table.
Don't start a bar's axis above zero or stretch a donut past ~7 slices.
Don't mix chart styles on one screen: every chart takes the shared grid, labels, Tooltip, legend and motion.

layout.title: Layout (Stack, Grid, Box, Container)
do: Build page structure with Stack and Grid and pick the gap by the relationship, the same step everywhere: 2xs inside one inline item, xs a thing and its label or a toolbar row, sm a group of Buttons or choices, md blocks inside one surface and stacked form fields, lg columns and groups inside a surface, xl page sections (Figma Master-Layout).
Step up one level at least between groups: the gap between groups is always larger than the gap inside them.
Use Stack direction="row" with justify="between" for a title + actions row.
Use Grid minColumnWidth for card grids so they reflow from phone to desktop.
Put a main column next to an aside with Grid columns={{ mobile: 1, desktop: "2fr 1fr" }} align="start"; on phones the aside moves under the main column.
Put page content in a Container so its margin follows the breakpoint.
Give a frame a surface only when it really is a separate layer; a Surface frame on a white (Alt) canvas needs border="pale".

Put the fill, stroke and corners of an auto layout frame on the Stack or Grid itself (Figma's frame with a fill is one layer): <Stack surface="surface" padding="lg" gap="md" radius="lg">, not a Box around a Stack.

Size like Figma auto layout: Hug for content-sized pieces, Fill for what takes the rest of a row or the full width (a main column; a Search next to buttons goes in a Box width="fill", since Search has no sizing props), maxWidth to cap a Fill line of text; use Fixed (a number) only for widths that really are fixed, such as a side column or a preview frame.

Pin a media overlay with position="absolute" and a constraint on token insets: a corner action on a photo is constraintX="right" insetRight="sm" constraintY="top" insetTop="sm"; a caption bar is constraintX="left-right" constraintY="bottom".
Put background media first and the content after it: the media is absolute (left-right × top-bottom), and the later in-flow content paints above it (Figma auto layout "Last on top").
Lift a Surface panel on Canvas/Default with effectStyle="Shadow/Bottom/Level-1" and no border: elevation follows the Sidebar, and it is the Card shadow.
Round only the top corners of top media to the container radius (radiusTopLeft and radiusTopRight), or clip the container; write radius plus only the corners that differ.
dont: Don't write display:flex / gap: 13px CSS for layout; use Stack/Grid and the scale.
Don't fix widths and heights in px to make a layout look right at one screen size; Hug and Fill reflow, Fixed does not (and a Fixed child never shrinks in a row).
Don't space the same relationship differently on different screens, or override a component's own padding or gap.
Don't make a Box clickable; clickable tiles are Card (or a Box with border="subtle" and role="button") (harness: box/border-matches-action).
Don't paint Canvas, Flat or Container on a Box: Canvas is the page, Flat is navigation, Container is modals and sheets.
Don't nest Containers.
Don't use position="absolute" for what gap, justify or alignSelf can do: an absolute layer leaves the flow and no longer reflows with its siblings.
Don't place status dots, badges or Card sub-actions by hand with absolute layers; they are component props (Avatar status, BadgeCounter, Card subAction).
Don't put a shadow on a tinted fill (Subtle, Pale, Surface-Alt) or on a Canvas/Alt page; there a closed border separates the box.
Don't write style={{ top }} or raw top/right/bottom/left/inset CSS in examples and templates; pin the layer with position, constraints and token insets (style-guard: position/token).

Don't mix radius="full" with a finite corner (radius="full" radiusBottomRight="xs"): full is 1000px, so the browser scales every corner down to fit and the small corner renders square. Use a finite radius (radius="xl" radiusBottomRight="xs"); full mixes only with none (harness: radius/full-mixed).

text.title: Text & Heading
do: Give a readout that changes in place (a zoom %, "3 of 12", a quantity between − and +) tabularNumbers and a minWidth, so the controls beside it stay put; keep a time or amount beside a row on one line with wrap={false}.

Colour emoji take the alpha of their text colour, so one in a light tone (Content/Neutral/Base or Light: captions, DescriptionList terms, muted text) renders faded: wrap the emoji alone in an opaque span, <Text as="span" textStyle=… tone="strongest">👋</Text>, and keep the words in the light tone (Zen has no Emoji component).

Give every page or screen exactly one h1, present at all times, that names it and matches document.title (plus the app name). Where the title is shown large (PageHeader, a phone large title) it is Heading/1, like the Figma Master-Layout page title, or a larger Display / Display-Extra style on an emphasis page (a home, a welcome, a storefront), never a smaller style (harness: heading/h1-is-heading-1); a compact app bar title is the screen's h1 and keeps its bar style (Body/Extra/Bold).

Follow the content hierarchy on the Typography page: page titles h1 Heading/1 (or larger: Display, Display-Extra); sections (a group of cards, a table, a list) h2 Heading/4; card and widget titles one level below the nearest heading above (h3 under a section, h2 right under the page title), always Heading/Subheading; a page title inside a tab (PageHeader headingLevel 2) h2 Heading/2; list group headers one level below the nearest heading above, Body/Small/Bold in tone "base" (a kicker label); overlay titles h2 by default (h1 also accepted), never Heading/1. On a phone the master screen's large title and a child screen's compact bar title are the h1, so content starts at h2 (audit: outline).

Step down one level at a time (h1 → h2 → h3); going back up may jump (h4 → h2). Every page or screen starts at h1; a component's headings take their level from where it is placed (headingLevel); fixed regions (Sidebar, Drawer) keep their level on every page.
Give the same kind of content the same style on a page, whatever its level, and mark up content that looks subordinate one level deeper.
Separate a section from the cards under it with spacing and containment (the card surface), not with a bigger style.

Emphasise inside a level with weight (Regular → Medium → Bold) and quiet secondary text with tone (light → base). Sizes stay as they are (a Zen rule; Apple also allows size). When weight carries a state (unread, new), say it in text too.
Use tone="base" for secondary copy and Body/Small meta, and "light" only for tertiary meta (timestamps, hints); Caption is always "light".
Use Text as="span" inside a line of other text or a flex row; the default p is a block.
Pluralise counts with plural(): "1 member", "12 members" (harness: copy/plural-count).

Mark the few words that need weight or colour inside a sentence with TextRun (<Text>Renews on <TextRun bold>Nov 2</TextRun></Text>), so the sentence stays one text for screen readers and translation; a link inside it is a Link.
dont: Don't pick a heading level for its size; set textStyle instead. A content h1 (the page title shown large) is never smaller than Heading/1: Heading/1, or a Display / Display-Extra style on an emphasis page.
Don't make a value (metric, price, count) a heading.

Don't let a heading look larger than the heading it sits under inside one content area (the page body, a card, an overlay); an app bar title and an overlay title are compared only within their own layer.
Don't colour body text with a colour family's Light token or a raw hex; use tone.
Don't truncate essential information without another way to read it (a tooltip or detail view).
Don't use TextRun outside a Text or Heading, or to set a whole text's style (set the Text's textStyle and tone instead).
Don't underline words to make them look like a link; a link is a Link.

app-shell.title: App Shell
do: Put one AppShell at the root of each app screen, inside ZenProvider, and pick the pattern from the screen's job (see Use).

With pattern="grid", build the page from Boxes and Flat Cards (MetricCard, ChartCard and Card keep theme flat) on the grey Canvas, and give Subtle only to a metric card that should stand out (◇ Master-Layout Rule, 16823:85229).

One elevation per screen, set by the Sidebar: Canvas default (grey) + the default Sidebar (Surface + shadow) + Shadow cards and panes; Canvas alt (white) + a Surface-alt or Flat Sidebar + bordered cards and panes (theme="border"); Canvas flat + a Flat Sidebar + bordered cards. Never a shadowed Sidebar on a white Canvas.

Lead the header's top row with Breadcrumbs (master={false} beside the toggle) or a Search, and keep its right side to utilities in this order: a plan Badge, AppShellAction buttons, the account menu last.
Put the page's PageHeader in the header's main (one h1) and its views (Tabs) in sections; the Body holds the content at the page margin, with no Container.
Give both side panes the same width (workspace and docs size them for you) and one theme.
Show unread items on the action itself (AppShellAction count or dot) so the count is also in its accessible name.
Store the rail state from onSidebarCollapsedChange so the Sidebar opens the way people left it.

For an app that runs on phones, give the shell its mobile parts mapped from the header: Sidebar rows → BottomNavigation (up to 5; more → the first 4 + More), Breadcrumbs → Back on a child screen, the PageHeader title → the TopNavigation title (large on a root), at most 3 trailing actions, the account → the avatar on a root (component-usage-rules §17).
dont: Don't build your own sidebar + main flex layout, your own panes or your own drawer.
Don't put primary page actions in the header's top row (harness: app-shell/primary-in-top-bar).
Don't put a Master crumb right after the header's collapse toggle: master={false}, or collapse="sidebar" (harness: app-shell/collapse-beside-master-crumb).
Don't give a pattern a part it does not draw, such as a trailingPane on sidebar (harness: app-shell/pattern-parts).
Don't nest AppShells (harness: app-shell/nested).
Don't repeat the Breadcrumbs in the PageHeader when the top row shows them (harness: app-shell/breadcrumbs-once).
Don't force layout in an app (harness: app-shell/forced-layout).
Don't put the PageHeader in the Body when the shell has a topNavigation: on a phone it stays beside the bar's title, two h1s (harness: app-shell/page-header-in-main).
Don't give the phone bar other words than the PageHeader title (harness: app-shell/top-navigation-title).

page-header.title: Page Header
do: Use exactly one PageHeader (one h1) per page.
Set document.title to the title, then the app name ("Invoices · Acme"), whenever the page changes (WCAG 2.4.2).
Start the page's sections at h2 Heading/4; a card right under the PageHeader takes an h2 in Heading/Subheading.
Order actions Tertiary first, Primary last, and keep one Primary (harness: page-header/one-primary).
Name Back after the destination ("Projects"), with the chevron icon; it is visible text (an icon-only TopNavigation Back is labelled "Back").
Keep the description to one or two sentences.
dont: Don't put more than one Primary in actions.
Don't use a heading level lower than 2 or skip the h1.
Don't repeat the title in the description.

dashboard-header.title: Dashboard Header
do: Inside an AppShell, put the rows in sections (Figma Header/Dashboard): the shell pads each row and keeps the top bar its own.
Give the Search a placeholder that names what it searches ("Search leave requests").
Make filters Chip variant="advanced" in controls, each opening its own Popover (harness: dashboard-header/filters-are-chips).
Write the result count with plural() and update it with the filters ("96 results", "1 result").
Pass the result count as plain text in subheading: the row draws it in Body/Base/Regular, the size of the text around it (user rule 2026-10-16; harness: dashboard-header/count-body).
Order actions Tertiary first and keep one Primary, last (harness: dashboard-header/one-primary).
Use only the props of the row's type: search on a navigation row does nothing (harness: dashboard-header/props-of-type).
dont: Don't use Buttons as filters in controls.
Don't make the result count a Heading or give it a heading or display text style: a count beside the filters is body text, not a title.
Don't put more than one Primary in actions.
Don't stack two navigation rows, or a navigation row under AppShell's top bar.
Don't leave type="main" without a title (harness: dashboard-header/main-needs-title).

form.title: Form
do: Bind fields with the helpers ({...form.field("email")}, {...form.selectField("role")}, {...form.checkboxField("terms")}); each one matches its field's own change signature.
Show an error when the user leaves a field with a bad value or submits, and clear it as soon as the value is fixed (useFormState does both).
Write each error as the fix: "Enter a valid email address, like name@company.com".
Group related fields in a Stack gap md (or a Grid columns={{ mobile: 1, desktop: 2 }}); Form spaces the groups lg.

Write Tertiary (Cancel) first and Primary (type="submit", named for the outcome) last in FormActions: Primary lands on the right, or on top when the actions stack (harness: form/actions-order, form/submit-button).
Give every FormFieldset a legend, and kind="radio" to a group of RadioButtons (harness: form-fieldset/needs-legend, form-fieldset/radio-kind).
Put field errors from the server on the field with setError; show a failed request (thrown by onSubmit, in submitError) in a Negative InlineMessage with a Try again action, keeping every value.
Show progress on the submit button while isSubmitting ("Saving…").
On a phone, use sticky FormActions so the main action stays above the home indicator while the fields scroll.
Mark the exception: when most fields are required, label only the optional ones (labelOptional / optional).

Using react-hook-form? Wrap each Zen field in its <Controller> and map value, the field's change callback (onValueChange(value) on every Zen field — or onChange(event) on the text fields — and onCheckedChange(checked) on Checkbox and Toggle), onBlur and error={fieldState.error?.message}; <Form onSubmit={handleSubmit(onValid)}> still focuses the first invalid field and announces the count.
dont: Don't disable the submit button until the form is valid; let people submit, then focus and explain the first problem.
Don't show an error while someone is still typing a new value; wait until they leave the field or submit.
Don't put Toggles in a Form that is saved later; use a Checkbox, and keep instant Toggles outside the Form (harness: form/toggle-outside-form).
Don't wrap InputField, SelectField & co. in FormField; they already have label, helpText and error.
Don't nest a Form inside a ModalForm that has onSubmit (nested forms); pass form.handleSubmit to ModalForm instead.
Don't clear the fields after a failed submit, and don't use the placeholder as the label or for instructions.

link.title: Link
do: Write link text that names the destination and makes sense on its own (“Billing settings”, “Status page”) (harness: link/vague-text).
Underline links inside running text with underline="always", so they never rely on colour alone.
Open other sites with external: it adds the icon, the hidden “(opens in a new tab)” and rel="noopener noreferrer" (harness: link/new-tab-is-external).
Render client-side routes with as={RouterLink}; the router's own props (to, replace) are forwarded.
Place a Link inside a Text or a line of copy: it takes that text style and size.
Keep tone="inherit" links underlined (the default for inherit) in legal lines, captions and footers (harness: link/inherit-needs-underline).
Turn on visited only for content people scan repeatedly, such as search results and docs.
dont: Don't use a Link for an action on the page (open a dialog, delete, save); that is a Button (harness: link/needs-href).
Don't write “click here”, “here”, “read more” or “learn more” as the whole link text (harness: link/vague-text).
Don't open a new tab with a bare target="_blank", and don't open pages of the same app in a new tab (harness: link/new-tab-is-external).
Don't remove the underline (underline="none") where nothing else says it is a link, such as inside a paragraph.
Don't put a Link inside a clickable row, card or button: nested interactive elements can't be reached reliably.

menu.title: Menu
do: Name an icon-only trigger after its object, aria-label="Actions for INV-1042"; the name also labels the menu.
Start labels with a verb and keep them to 1–3 words; end with “…” only when the action asks for more input (Move to…).
Group related actions under MenuGroup headings or between separators; put destructive actions last, marked danger.
Keep an action that is unavailable right now visible but disabled, with a caption that says why.
Use align="end" when the trigger sits at the right end of a row or card.
Confirm a destructive choice in a negative Dialog, or offer Undo, after the menu closes; focus returns to the trigger.
Put menus straight into Table rows and Cards: the menu floats in the overlay layer, so overflow never clips it.
On a phone, keep menus to a few short actions; longer lists, or ones that need a title, are an Action BottomSheet.
dont: Don't use a Menu to pick a value or show a checked state; that is SelectField, Segmented or a Chip + Popover (harness: menu/not-for-selection).
Don't render a Menu without a trigger (harness: menu/needs-trigger), and don't open it on hover.
Don't put inputs, toggles or several lines of text inside menu items.
Don't open a menu from a menu item; open a Dialog or SidePanel for the next step.
Don't hide the one action people use most behind ⋯; show it as a button.
Don't mix items with and without icons in one menu.

provider.title: ZenProvider (app root)
do: Wrap the app in exactly one root ZenProvider and import "@zen-ds/react/styles.css" once.
Build phone apps with typography="mobile" (and density="comfortable" when targets are touch-first).
Offer light/dark with theme="system" or a toggle that sets theme; never hard-code dark colours.
Nest a provider to switch a region's mode; unset props inherit from the parent.
Render overlays (Dialog, Toast, Menu…) anywhere inside the provider: they portal into its root and keep its modes.

Set locale="vi" (or your app's language) once on the root: every Zen component's built-in text follows it; override single strings with labels={{ … }} and use a component's own prop (closeLabel, placeholder, aria-label) only for one-off wording.
dont: Don't set data-theme or data-density on elements by hand, or paint the page background yourself.
Don't wrap every component in its own provider; one root plus the few regions that really switch modes.
Don't give a nested provider paint when it only changes typography or density inside a card; pass paint={false}.

description-list.title: Description List
do: Keep one end edge (user, 2026-10-04 / 10-06): every row ends on the list's end edge. A row action sits Gap/XSmall (8px) after its own value and takes room only in its row, as an iOS value cell with an accessory and Figma's Item (Content · Action): a row without an action keeps its value on the edge, so Copy on one DNS value next to Type and Host is fine. A Flat icon action lines its icon, not its 32px box, up with the edge. Amounts that add up to a total take no row actions (they must share one edge with the total): a one-off action there (remove a discount) is a removable Badge beside the term.
Use inline for short values (amounts, dates, statuses) and layout="stacked" for long ones (addresses, emails, notes).
Format every value for people: currency with its symbol, dates written out ("2 October 2026"), IDs as users see them.
Close a calculation with one emphasis row, the total; the rows above it stay regular (harness: description-list/one-emphasis).
Keep terms short nouns in a stable order across screens (Subtotal, Shipping, Tax, Total).
Name row actions with their row: `Edit<VisuallyHidden> email</VisuallyHidden>` or `aria-label="Copy order number"`.
Put the list inside a Card, Side Panel or Bottom Sheet body; it takes the container's width and stacks on its own when narrow.
dont: Don't use it for data people scan across records or sort; use a Table.
Don't emphasise more than one row, or colour values beyond a status (a positive discount, a negative balance).
Don't add Divider elements inside the list; use divider (a dl only holds dt/dd groups).
Don't give a row more than one action, or a Primary button.
Don't truncate values; long values wrap, or use layout="stacked".

action-bar.title: Action Bar
do: Hold one Primary, the screen's main action (harness: action-bar/one-primary).

On phones pick the direction by the actions: vertical when one main action leads (Add to cart, with Save for later below: Large full-width, Primary on top); horizontal when the two are a pair people choose between (Clear all · Show 6 prints, Decline · Accept: two Large buttons, Primary at the end) (harness: action-bar/full-width-size, action-bar/primary-order).
Prefer primaryAction / secondaryAction: they get the right size and order in both directions, so one set of actions serves phone and desktop.
Place a sticky bar as the last child of the scrolling content, inside the form it submits (type: "submit").
Say what the actions act on in the summary ("2 prints · $96.00", "3 unsaved changes") and announce changes with role="status".
Disable the Primary only while its precondition is unmet, and say why in the summary ("No changes to save yet").
dont: Don't put two Primary buttons in the bar, or a Secondary as the alternative.
Don't use small buttons (2xs · xs · sm) in a vertical bar; stretched thin buttons read as fields.
Don't add a drop shadow or a tinted fill; the Pale top rule separates the bar.
Don't stack more than two actions on a phone; move the rest into the page or a More menu.
Don't use surface="none" on a sticky or fixed bar; the content would scroll visibly under the buttons.
Don't pad the page for the home indicator yourself; the bar already clears the safe area.

image.title: Image & Thumbnail
do: Use frame={false} for a cut-out picture on a transparent background (a mascot, a product without its backdrop): the frame would show as a faint square around it.
Always pass alt: what the picture shows in context; alt="" only when it is decorative or text beside it names it (harness: image/needs-alt).
Set ratio so the frame keeps its size while loading and nothing jumps when the picture arrives.
Use loading="eager" only for the first picture on screen; keep the rest lazy.
Use Thumbnail md (40) in ListItem leading slots, sm (32) in captioned Table cells and xs (24) in plain ones.
When a picture fails, keep the frame and offer a way forward nearby (Try again, Replace).
Use fit="contain" for logos, documents and cut-outs that must not be cropped.
dont: Don't use a file name or "image of…" as alt (harness: image/alt-describes).
Don't repeat the caption or the row title in alt; screen readers would read it twice.
Don't size a picture with a fixed width and height; give it a ratio and let it fill its container.
Don't use Thumbnail for people; Avatar has initials, status and stacks.
Don't put text over a picture without a scrim or an overlay type that keeps it readable.

visually-hidden.title: Visually Hidden
do: Start hidden text that continues a visible label with a space and no punctuation (`Edit<VisuallyHidden> email</VisuallyHidden>`) so the name reads as one phrase.
Render a status region from the start, empty, then change its text; a region inserted together with its message is often not announced.
Make the skip link the first focusable element of the page and point it at the main content (`tabIndex={-1}`).
Keep the visible label inside the accessible name (WCAG 2.5.3): add words, never replace them.
dont: Don't hide a link or control without focusable; keyboard users would land on something invisible (harness: visually-hidden/focusable-shows).
Don't stuff keywords or long instructions into hidden text; screen-reader users hear every word.
Don't use display:none, visibility:hidden or the hidden attribute for screen-reader text; they remove it from the accessibility tree.
Don't hide a heading sighted people need too; show it.
